column17: 她出现在聚会上——你听好了——穿着一件价值3,000美元的名牌设计师礼服！

column10: used to talk about the result or effect of something that may happen or be true
column11: 用于谈论某件可能发生或可能为真的事情的结果或影响
column12: If it rains, (then) we won't go to the park.
column13: 如果下雨，我们就不去公园。
column14: If he actually did commit the crime, he deserves to be punished.
column15: 如果他确实犯了罪，他就应该受到惩罚。
column16: If you believe that, you'll believe anything!
column17: 如果你相信那个，你什么都能相信！
column18:
Come to the party if you can.
If you really want to know, you should ask.
What will happen if I fail the test?
You should study. If not, you won't pass the test. = If you don't (study), you won't pass the test.
Please arrive early if possible. = Please arrive early if it is possible.
I'll do the work myself if necessary. = I'll do the work myself if it is necessary.
If and when he comes, you can ask him. = When and if he comes, you can ask him.
column19:
如果你能来，就来参加聚会吧。
如果你真的想知道，你应该去问。
如果我考试不及格会发生什么？
你应该学习。如果不学习，你就不会通过考试。
如果可能的话，请早点到。
如果有必要，我会自己做这项工作。
如果他来了，你可以问他。

column10: used to discuss the imaginary result or effect of something that did not happen or that is or was not true
column11: 用于讨论某些没有发生或不真实的事情的假想结果或影响
column12: If you had studied, you would have passed the test.
column13: 如果你当时学习了，你就会通过考试。
column14: The situation would be funny if it weren't so tragic. = (informal) The situation would be funny if it wasn't so tragic.
column15: 如果不是那么悲惨，这种情况本来会很可笑。
column16: The harvest would have been good if it had rained.
column17: 如果下雨的话，收成本来会很好。
column18: The news would be interesting if (it were) true, but it's not true.
column19: 如果这条新闻是真的，那会很有趣，但它并不是真的。

column10: used to say that something must happen before another thing can happen
column11: 用来说某事必须在另一件事发生之前发生。
column12: He said he'll come to the party if she comes too. = (more strongly) He said he'll come to the party only if she comes too. = (most strongly) He says he'll come to the party if and only if she comes too.
column13: 他说如果她也来，他就会来参加聚会。

column10: used to indicate a result that always occurs when something happens
column11: 用于表示每当某事发生时总会出现的结果
column12: He gets angry if [=when] you disagree with him.
column13: 如果你不同意他，他会生气。
column14: The engine stalls if you let it get too hot.
column15: 如果让发动机过热，它就会熄火。

column10: even though although
column11: 即使 虽然
column12: It was an interesting if unbelievable story.
column13: 这是一个有趣但难以置信的故事。
column14: Her actions were understandable, if not forgivable.
column15: 她的行为可以理解，尽管未必可以原谅。
column16: He had to perform an annoying, if necessary, task.
column17: 他不得不执行一项令人烦恼但又必要的任务。
column18:
a fair, if tough, boss
The weather was good, if not great.
column19:
一个公正但严格的老板
天气还不错，虽然算不上很好。

column10: used to introduce a statement or question about something that is not certain
column11: 用于引出关于某些不确定事情的陈述或问题
column12: I'll see if [=whether] I can come.
column13: 我会看看我是否能来。
column14: Do you know if he'll come to the party?
column15: 你知道他会来参加聚会吗？
column16: I wonder if it's true (or not).
column17: 我想知道这是否是真的（或者不是）。
column18:
Frankly, I doubt if he'll pass the exams.
She asked if the mail had come.
We should determine/decide if it is safe to go swimming.
column19:
坦率地说，我怀疑他是否能通过考试。
她问邮件是否已经到了。
我们应该确定/决定是否可以安全游泳。

column10: used to make a polite request or suggestion
column11: 用于提出礼貌的请求或建议
column12: Would you mind if I sat here? [=may I sit here?]
column13: 你介意我坐这里吗？
column14: If you will/would (be good enough to) follow me, ladies and gentlemen, I'll take you to your seats.
column15: 各位女士们、先生们，如果您愿意跟我来，我会带您到您的座位。
column16: If I could make a suggestion, why don't we sit closer to the front of the theater?
column17: 如果我可以提个建议，我们为什么不坐到剧院前面一点呢？
column18: I'd like to stay a little longer, if you don't mind. = I'd like to stay a little longer, if it's/that's all right with you.
column19: 如果你不介意的话，我想再待一会儿。

column10: used to state an opinion in a polite way
column11: 用于以礼貌的方式表达意见
column12: You're looking particularly lovely today, if I may say so.
column13: 如果我可以说的话，你今天看起来格外迷人。

column10: used in statements that describe feelings (such as regret) about a possible situation
column11: 用于描述对某种可能情况的感受（如遗憾）的陈述中
column12: I'm sorry if you think I insulted you.
column13: 如果你觉得我侮辱了你，我很抱歉。
column14: I'd be sorry if you thought I had insulted you.
column15: 如果你认为我侮辱了你，我会感到抱歉。
column16: I don't care if we're late.
column17: 我不在乎我们是否迟到了。

column10: used in statements and questions that express doubt
column11: 用于表达怀疑的陈述和疑问句中
column12: I met Brenda last week—if that is/was in fact her real name.
column13: 我上周遇到了布伦达——如果那真的是她的真名的话。
column14: If you're so smart, why aren't you rich?
column15: 如果你这么聪明，为什么不富有？

column10: used to introduce an even stronger alternative to what has just been said
column11: 用于引出比刚才所说内容更有力的另一种选择
column12: These changes will have little if any impact on the problem.
column13: 这些变化对问题几乎没有影响，或者根本没有影响。
column14: Few if any of the town's original settlers are left.
column15: 镇上最初的定居者几乎都已经不在了。
column16: Rarely, if ever, does that happen.
column17: 那种情况几乎从未发生过。
column18:
His efforts have helped to save thousands, if not millions, of lives.
My car is as fast as yours if not (even) faster.
column19:
他的努力帮助拯救了成千上万，甚至可能是数百万人的生命。
如果不是更快的话，我的车和你的一样快。

column10: used to express surprise about meeting someone when it is not expected
column11: 用来表达在意想不到的情况下遇到某人时的惊讶
column12: So I went to the game and who should I see there if not [=but] my old friend Tom!
column13: 所以我去了比赛，结果你猜我在那里遇到了谁？不是别人，正是我的老朋友汤姆！
column14: Well, if it isn't my old friend Tom!
column15: 哎呀，这不是我的老朋友汤姆吗！
column16: So I went to the game and who did I see there if it wasn't my old friend Tom!
column17: 所以我去了比赛，结果你猜我在那里遇到了谁？竟然是我老朋友汤姆！

column10: used to emphasize the truth of a statement
column11: 用于强调某个陈述的真实性
column12: The idea is true if any idea has ever been! [=the idea is certainly true]
column13: 这个观点如果有任何观点曾经真实过，那它就是真的！
column14: “He claims that he's never met her.” “Well, if that isn't the biggest load of nonsense I've ever heard!” [=that is a lot of nonsense; that is completely untrue]
column15: “他说他从未见过她。” “哼，这简直是我听过的最大的一派胡言！”
column16: I'll get my revenge if it's the last thing I do! [=I am determined to get my revenge]
column17: 就算是我做的最后一件事，我也要报仇！

column10: something that is not certain something that could either happen or not happen
column11: 某件不确定的事情，可能会发生，也可能不会发生。
column12: There are too many ifs in this proposal.
column13: 这个提案里有太多的假设。
column14: They could win if everyone plays his best, but that's a big if. [=it is not likely that everyone will play his best]
column15: 如果每个人都发挥出最佳水平，他们可能会赢，但这是个很大的假设。
column16: (US) She's the most qualified candidate, and there are no ifs, ands, or buts about it! = (Brit) She's the most qualified candidate, and there are no ifs and buts about it! [=it is certain that she is the most qualified candidate]
column17: （美）她是最有资格的候选人，这一点毫无疑问！

column10: used to indicate what someone said or thought about what was going to happen or be done
column11: 用来表示某人对将要发生或将要做的事情所说或所想的内容。
column12: She said she would be leaving soon. [=she said, “I will be leaving soon”]
column13: 她说她很快就要离开了。
column14: She said (that) she would help me with my project.
column15: 她说她会帮我做我的项目。
column16: He thought (that) the drive would take about two hours.
column17: 他认为这段路程大约需要两个小时。
column18:
I had no idea where the path would lead me.
They knew (that) I would enjoy the trip.
I never thought that she would lie to me.
column19:
我完全不知道这条路会把我带到哪里。
他们知道我会喜欢这次旅行。
我从没想过她会对我撒谎。

column10: used to talk about a possible situation that has not happened or that you are imagining
column11: 用于谈论尚未发生或你正在想象的可能情况
column12: You would look good in a tuxedo.
column13: 你穿西装会很好看。
column14: If I could leave work early, I would.
column15: 如果我能早点下班，我会的。
column16: It would be a shame to miss the party.
column17: 错过这个聚会就太可惜了。
column18:
What would you do if you won the lottery?
You would be stupid to quit your job. = It would be stupid (of you) to quit your job. [=if you quit your job, you will be doing something stupid]
Things would be different if I still had that job.
If you lived closer, I would see you every day.
If they were coming, they would be here by now.
column19:
如果你中了彩票，你会做什么？
你要是辞职就太傻了。
如果我还保有那份工作，情况就会不一样。
如果你住得近些，我每天都会见到你。
如果他们要来，现在应该已经到了。

column10: used with have to talk about something that did not happen or was not done
column11: 与 have 连用，用于谈论某事没有发生或没有被做。
column12: She would have won the race if she hadn't tripped.
column13: 如果她没有绊倒，她本来会赢得比赛。
column14: I would have stopped by your house had I known you were home.
column15: 如果我知道你在家，我本来会顺路去你家的。
column16: If you had told me that you were coming, I would have picked you up at the airport.
column17: 如果你早告诉我你要来，我就会去机场接你。

column10: used to say what you think someone should do or to ask for someone's opinion about what to do
column11: 用来表达你认为某人应该做什么，或者用来询问某人对该做什么的看法。
column12: If I were you, I would go to the hospital. [=I think that you should go to the hospital]
column13: 如果我是你，我会去医院。
column14: I would take the train instead of driving into the city.
column15: 我会选择乘火车而不是开车进城。
column16: I would turn back if I were you.
column17: 如果我是你，我会回头。
column18: What would you do in my situation?
column19: 如果你处在我的处境，你会怎么做？

column10: used to say that you want to do or have something
column11: 用来说你想做某事或想要某物
column12: We would like to help [=we want to help] in any way we can.
column13: 我们希望以任何我们能做到的方式提供帮助。
column14: I'd like to help, but I'm too busy.
column15: 我很想帮忙，但我太忙了。
column16: She would like to attend college, but she can't afford it right now.
column17: 她想上大学，但她现在负担不起。
column18:
I would rather have ice cream than cheesecake. = (more commonly) I'd rather have ice cream than cheesecake.
I'd rather not go out this evening. [=I don't want to go out this evening]
I would sooner die than be enslaved.
I'd sooner starve than eat that disgusting food.
column19:
我宁愿吃冰淇淋也不想吃芝士蛋糕。
我今晚宁愿不出去。
我宁愿死也不愿被奴役。
我宁愿饿死也不吃那种恶心的食物。

column11: 用于提出礼貌性问题，或提出礼貌性的请求、提议、邀请等。
column12: Would you please help us?
column13: 您能帮帮我们吗？
column14: Would you care for some tea?
column15: 您想喝点茶吗？
column16: She asked if I would have dinner with her.
column17: 她问我是否愿意和她一起吃晚饭。

Would you mind making a little less noise? = Please make a little less noise, would you?

Would it be all right if we left a little early?

你介意小声一点吗？
请这边走，好吗？
我们早点离开可以吗？
我想看一下酒单。
你愿意和我一起吃晚饭吗？
有人还要咖啡吗？

column10: used to say that you are willing to do something
column11: 用来说你愿意做某事

column13: “你会帮他吗？”“不会，我绝对不会！”
column14: The doctor will see you now.
column15: 医生现在会见你。
column16: I would do anything to protect my children.
column17: 我愿意做任何事情来保护我的孩子。
column18:
Yes, I will marry you.
No one would do it.

column19:
是的，我愿意嫁给你。
没有人会这么做。
我很乐意帮忙。

column11: 用于否定句中，表示某人不愿意做某事。
column12: He would not help us. = (more commonly) He wouldn't help us. [=he refused to help us]
column13: 他不会帮我们。

column10: used to express a wish
column11: 用来表达愿望
column12: I wish that he would call me more often. = I wish he'd call me more often.
column13: 我希望他能更经常给我打电话。

column10: used to express your opinion
column11: 用来表达你的观点
column12: I would hate to have that job.
column13: 我可不想做那份工作。
column14: I would love to be in her position.
column15: 我很想处在她的位置。

column10: used to talk about something that always or often happened in the past
column11: 用来谈论过去总是或经常发生的事情

column13: 当我的朋友还住在这里时，我们每天都会一起吃午饭。
column14: She would always take the nine o'clock bus. = She'd always take the nine o'clock bus.
column15: 她总是乘坐九点钟的公交车。

column11: 与 so (that) 连用，用于解释为什么做某事

column13: 我小心地包装了花瓶，以便它能在旅途中完好无损。
column14: We left early so we would be sure to arrive on time.
column15: 我们早早出发，这样就能确保准时到达。

column10: used to say what you think is probably true
column11: 用来表达你认为很可能是真的事情
column12: I would say that he looks to be around sixty. [=he looks like he might be sixty years old, but I'm not sure]
column13: 我会说他看起来大约六十岁。
column14: I would think/hope that he was telling the truth, but I really don't know.
column15: 我会认为/希望他说的是真的，但我真的不知道。
column16: “How long will it take?” “I would imagine it will take about an hour.”
column17: “需要多长时间？”“我想大概需要一个小时。”

column10: used to say that something is possible or likely
column11: 用来说某事是可能的或有可能发生的
column12: I think my swimming pool would [=could] hold 20,000 gallons of water.
column13: 我认为我的游泳池可以容纳20,000加仑的水。

column10: used to express your displeasure with behavior that you think is typical of someone
column11: 用来表达你对某人典型行为的不满。
column12: “He said that you were the one who made the mistake.” “He would say that, wouldn't he? What a jerk.”
column13: “他说是你犯了错。” “他当然会这么说，不是吗？真是个混蛋。”

column10:
[usually + that]
used to say that you wish something was true, had happened, etc.
column11: 用于表示你希望某事是真的、已经发生了等。

column13: 我真希望我能再年轻一次。
column14: I would [=wish] that he had lived. = Would that he had lived.
column15: 我真希望他还活着。

relating to or belonging to a certain woman, girl, or female animal; made or done by a certain woman, girl, or female animal
column11: 与某个女性、女孩或雌性动物有关或属于她们的；由某个女性、女孩或雌性动物制造或完成的

column13: 她买了自己的房子。
column14: Her parents will visit soon.
column15: 她的父母很快就会来拜访。

column17: 她叫什么名字？

I would like to read some of her essays.

the United States and her allies
column19:
我想读一些她的散文。
她因犯罪被监禁。
轮到她上场了。
这艘船正在港口修理船体。
美国及其盟友

column10: used to refer to a certain woman, girl, or female animal as the object of a verb or a preposition
column11: 用来指代某个女人、女孩或雌性动物，作为动词或介词的宾语。

column13: 这件连衣裙她妹妹穿着也合身。
column14: I gave the book to her.
column15: 我把书给了她。

column17: 送给她的礼物
column18:
Did you invite her?
Tell her I said hello.
column19:
你邀请她了吗？
替我向她问好。

column10: the whole, entire, total amount, quantity, or extent of
column11: 全部、整个、总量、数量或范围
column12: He stayed awake all night. [=the whole/entire night]
column13: 他整晚都没睡。
column14: She worked hard all day. [=throughout the entire day]
column15: 她一整天都在努力工作。
column16: I've been waiting all week to see her.
column17: 我整整等了一周才见到她。
column18:
He had to walk all the way home.
She works all year round.
He'll need all the help he can get.
Someone took all the candy.
It was one of the greatest victories of all time. [=one of the greatest victories ever]
I think about her all the time. [=I think about her constantly]
column19:
他不得不一路走回家。
她全年都在工作。
他需要尽可能多的帮助。
有人把所有的糖果都拿走了。
那是有史以来最伟大的胜利之一。
我一直都在想她。

column10:
[used with a plural noun or pronoun to mean that a statement is true of every person or thing in a group]
every member or part of
column11: 每个成员或部分

column13: 我所有的朋友都在那里。
column14: a film suitable for all ages
column15: 一部适合所有年龄段观看的电影
column16: They all came late.
column17: 他们都来晚了。
column18:
We all need to work faster.
I read all the magazines. = I read them all.
All these eggs are ready.
“…all men are created equal…”
She thinks all teenagers are alike. = She thinks teenagers are all alike.
Not all teenagers are alike. = Teenagers are not all alike.
They serve breakfast at all hours. [=at any hour, at any time of day]
They were up till/until all hours. [=they were up very late]
She has to deal with all kinds/sorts/types of people. [=with people of every kind/sort/type]
column19:
我们都需要更快地工作。
我读了所有的杂志。
这些鸡蛋都准备好了。
“……人人生而平等……”
她认为所有青少年都一样。
并不是所有青少年都一样。
他们全天供应早餐。
他们一直熬夜到很晚。
她必须应对各种各样的人。

column10:
[used with a plural noun or pronoun to mean that a statement is true of a group of people or things considered together]
the whole number or sum of
column11: 总数；总和
column12: It was great to see him again after all these years.
column13: 多年以后再次见到他，真是太好了。

column10: any whatever
column11: 任何，无论什么

column13: 他的罪行毫无疑问。
column14: She denied all [=any] responsibility for the accident.
column15: 她否认对这起事故负有任何责任。

column10:
[used to indicate the manner in which something is done]
as much as possible of (something)

column13: 他完全认真/天真地说话。

column11: 只具有或显示（某种品质、特征等）

column13: 当老师进来时，学生们立刻全神贯注。

column15: 他在老板面前一直笑容满面。

column10: near or not far from (something) in time
column11: 在时间上接近或不远于（某事物）
column12: a night about [=around] midsummer
column13: 仲夏夜左右

column10: in the area near to (something or someone)
column11: 在（某物或某人）附近的区域
column12: Fish are abundant about [=around] the reefs.
column13: 鱼在珊瑚礁周围很丰富。

column10: over or in different parts of (a place)
column11: 在（某地）的各处或不同部分
column12: He's a well-known figure about [=around, throughout] the town.
column13: 他是全镇有名的人物。
column14: He traveled all about [=around] the country.
column15: 他走遍了全国。

column10: on every side of (something or someone)
column11: 在（某物或某人）的每一侧
column12: They wrapped the blanket about [=around] her.
column13: 他们用毯子裹住了她。
column14: A crowd gathered about [=around] him.
column15: 一群人聚集在他周围。

column10: used to say that something is done quickly or slowly
column11: 用来说某事做得快或慢
column12: He was slow about doing his work. [=he did his work slowly]
column13: 他做工作很慢。
column14: If you're going to do that, you need to be quick about it. [=you need to do it quickly]
column15: 如果你要那样做，你得快点。

column10: in the act or process of doing (something)
column11: 在做（某事）的行为或过程中
column12: Do it well while you're about it. [=while you're at it]
column13: 趁你正在做的时候，把它做好。
column14: He seems to know what he's about. [=to know what he's doing]
column15: 他似乎很懂行。

column10:
[often + how, why, where, etc.] [often + about]
to have (information of some kind) in your mind
column11: 在你的脑海中拥有（某种信息）
column12: He knows a lot about the history of the town.
column13: 他对这个小镇的历史非常了解。
column14: Do you know the answer?
column15: 你知道答案吗？
column16: I don't know her name.
column17: 我不知道她的名字。
column18:
Do you know what time it is?
I don't know the words to that song.
They knew a good deal about the problem.
She knows the rules of the game.
He knows everything about horses. = He knows all/everything there is to know about horses.
Do you know why she left this suitcase here?
Do you know where she went?
No one knows (for sure) how long it will take to fix the problem.
He knows perfectly/full well how to do it.
If you want the answer, ask someone who knows.
“What is she doing?” “Believe me, you don't want to know.” [=you would be shocked or upset to learn what she is doing]
He knows (all) about horses.
column19:
你知道现在几点了吗？
我不知道那首歌的歌词。
他们对这个问题了解很多。
她知道这项游戏的规则。
他对马了如指掌。
你知道她为什么把这个手提箱留在这里吗？
你知道她去哪儿了吗？
没有人（能确定）需要多长时间才能解决这个问题。
他非常清楚怎么做这件事。
如果你想要答案，就去问一个知道的人。
“她在做什么？” “相信我，你不想知道。”
他对马非常了解。

column10:
[usually + how, why, where, etc.]
to understand (something) to have a clear and complete idea of (something)
column11: 理解（某事），对（某事）有清晰而完整的认识
column12: I don't know much about art, but I know what I like.
column13: 我对艺术了解不多，但我知道自己喜欢什么。
column14: Scientists don't yet know why this happens.
column15: 科学家们还不知道为什么会发生这种情况。
column16: I don't know what to do.
column17: 我不知道该怎么办。
column18:
I don't know what you want me to do.
We had almost no money in those days. I don't know how we managed.
I don't know how you could be so careless.
You know perfectly/full well what I am trying to say.
“How could she do that?” “How should/would I know?!” [=I don't know, and you should not expect me to know]
column19:
我不知道你想让我做什么。
那时候我们几乎没有钱。我不知道我们是怎么撑过来的。
我不知道你怎么会这么粗心。
你完全清楚我在说什么。
“她怎么能那样做？” “我怎么会知道？！”

column10:
[often + how]
to have learned (something, such as a skill or a language)
column11: 学会了（某事，比如一项技能或一门语言）
column12: She knows karate/CPR.
column13: 她会空手道/心肺复苏。
column14: He knows Spanish.
column15: 他会西班牙语。
column16: Do you know how to type?
column17: 你会打字吗？
column18: I would go swimming with you, but I don't know how (to swim). [=I never learned to swim]
column19: 我本来可以和你一起去游泳，但我不会游泳。

column10:
[often + about or of]
to be aware of (something) to realize (something)
column11: 意识到（某事），认识到（某事）
column12: She knows that many people will not believe her.
column13: 她知道很多人不会相信她。
column14: I know (that) this isn't easy for you, but you have to keep trying.
column15: 我知道这对你来说并不容易，但你必须继续努力。
column16: As soon as I turned on the light I knew that something was missing.
column17: 我一开灯就知道有什么东西不见了。
column18:
There was no way for me to know that he was your brother. = How was I to know that he was your brother?
It's wrong and you know it! [=you are aware that it is wrong]
“I'm sorry I threw out those bags.” “It's okay: you couldn't have known that I needed them.” = “It's okay: you had no way of knowing that I needed them.” = (Brit) “It's okay: you weren't to know that I needed them.”
You ought to know by now that she is always late.
It's impossible to know what will happen next. = There's no way of knowing what will happen next. = There's no knowing what will happen next.
If you've never been to Venice, you don't know what you're missing. [=you would enjoy going to Venice very much]
You know as well as I do that they expect us at 8:00.
You don't know how happy I am to see you. [=I am extremely happy to see you]
You'll never know what this means to me. = You can't know how much this means to me. [=this means a great deal to me]
As far as I know, they plan to arrive on Monday. [=I believe that they plan to arrive on Monday, but I am not sure]
We're planning a party for George. As you know, he'll be leaving the company next month.
I knew about the problem. [=I was aware of the problem]
Does she know about the meeting?
I don't know of any job openings right now. [=I am not aware of any job openings right now]
I know of her as a poet but not as a novelist. [=I am familiar with her poetry but not with her novels]
Do you know of a good lawyer? [=can you recommend a good lawyer?]
“Does he have relatives nearby?” “Not that I know of.” [=I don't think he has any relatives nearby]
column19:
我根本不可能知道他是你哥哥。
这是错的，你自己也知道！
“对不起，我把那些袋子扔了。” “没关系：你不可能知道我需要它们。”
你现在应该知道她总是迟到了。
根本无法知道接下来会发生什么。
如果你从没去过威尼斯，你就不知道你错过了什么。
你和我一样清楚，他们希望我们八点到。
你不知道见到你我有多高兴。
你永远不会知道这对我意味着什么。
据我所知，他们计划周一到达。
我们正在为乔治筹备一个聚会。你也知道，他下个月就要离开公司了。
我知道这个问题。
她知道会议的事吗？
我现在不知道有任何职位空缺。
我知道她是诗人，但不知道她是小说家。
你知道有好的律师吗？
“他附近有亲戚吗？” “据我所知没有。”

column10: to be certain of (something)
column11: 确定（某事）
column12: Everyone else believes him, but I just know (that) he's lying.
column13: 其他人都相信他，但我就是知道他在说谎。
column14: I don't know if I can trust her. [=I am not sure that I can trust her]
column15: 我不知道我是否能信任她。
column16: It's hard to know exactly where the candidate stands on this issue.
column17: 很难确切知道这位候选人在这个问题上的立场。
column18:
I knew he'd forget.
I need to know if they are coming.
“She says she's not coming.” “I knew it!” [=I was sure that she wouldn't come]
I knew it all along. [=I was always sure of it]
“They're coming.” “Do you know [=are you certain], or are you just guessing?” = “Do you know for sure/certain, or are you just guessing?”
He thinks he got the job but he doesn't know for sure.
column19:
我就知道他会忘记。
我需要知道他们是否会来。
“她说她不来了。”“我就知道！”
我一直都知道。
“他们要来。”“你确定吗，还是只是猜的？”
他以为自己得到了这份工作，但他并不确定。

column10: to have met and talked to (someone) to be acquainted or familiar with (a person)
column11: 见过并与（某人）交谈过，对（某人）有所了解或熟悉
column12: “Do you know Clara?” “Yes, we've met.”
column13: “你认识克拉拉吗？”“是的，我们见过面。”
column14: “Do you know Clara?” “We've met but I wouldn't say that I really know her.” [=I am not close to her; I don't know much about her]
column15: “你认识克拉拉吗？” “我们见过面，但我不敢说真的认识她。”
column16: I've known him for years. He's one of my best friends.
column17: 我认识他已经很多年了。他是我最好的朋友之一。
column18:
Knowing you, you'll be the first one there. [=because I know you so well, I expect you to be the first one there]
She's the kindest person I know.
To know him is to love him. [=the people who know him feel great affection for him]
We just bought a house here last month, and we're still getting to know our neighbors. [=we're still meeting our neighbors; we're still becoming acquainted with our neighbors]
column19:
了解你的人都知道，你一定会第一个到。
她是我认识的人中最善良的。
认识他就是爱上他。
我们上个月刚在这里买了房子，还在慢慢认识邻居。

column10: to have experience with (something) to be acquainted or familiar with (something)
column11: 有……的经验，对……熟悉或了解
column12: She knows the city very well.
column13: 她非常熟悉这座城市。
column14: Do you know her painting/writing/work?
column15: 你知道她的画作/写作/作品吗？
column16: Do you know any good restaurants in this area?
column17: 你知道这个地区有什么好的餐厅吗？
column18:
We're still getting to know the neighborhood.
The building as we know it [=as it exists now] is quite different from how it looked when it was first built.
This is the end of the organization as we know it. [=the organization has changed and will never again be the same as it was]
column19:
我们还在熟悉这个社区。
我们现在所了解的大楼与最初建成时的样子大不相同。
这就是我们所熟知的组织的终结。

column10:
[usually used as known]
to have experienced (something)
column11: 经历过（某事）
column12: someone who knows grief well [=someone who has experienced a lot of grief]
column13: 非常了解悲伤的人
column14: I've known failure and I've known success. [=I have failed and I have succeeded]
column15: 我经历过失败，也经历过成功。

column10: to recognize (someone or something) to identify (someone or something) accurately
column11: 识别（某人或某物）；准确地辨认（某人或某物）
column12: “How will I know her?” “She'll be wearing a red sweater.”
column13: “我怎么认出她？” “她会穿一件红色毛衣。”
column14: I would know [=recognize] that voice anywhere.
column15: 我无论在哪里都能认出那声音。
column16: I know his face [=his face is familiar to me] but I don't remember his name.
column17: 我认得他的脸，但我不记得他的名字。
column18:
I feel like I know this house, but I've never been here before.
I know many of the customers at the café by sight. [=I see them often enough that I recognize them]
column19:
我觉得我认识这栋房子，但我以前从没来过这里。
我在咖啡馆里能认出很多顾客的面孔。

column10: to recognize the difference between two things to be able to distinguish (one thing) from another
column11: 识别两件事物之间的区别，能够将（一件事物）与另一件事物区分开来。
column12: know right from wrong
column13: 明辨是非

column10:
[usually followed by to + verb]
to be sure that (someone or something) has a particular quality, character, etc., because of your experiences with that person or thing
column11: 由于你与某人或某事的经历，确信（某人或某事）具有某种特质、性格等。
column12: I've worked with him for many years, and I know him to be an honest man.
column13: 我和他共事多年，我知道他是个诚实的人。
column14: I know the business to be legitimate.
column15: 我知道这家公司是合法的。

column10:
[+ as] [often used as (be) known as]
to think of (someone or something) as having a particular quality, character, etc.
column11: 将（某人或某事）视为具有某种特质、性格等。
column12: His neighbors knew him as a quiet and friendly person, but the people he worked with saw a different side of him.
column13: 他的邻居们认为他是一个安静友好的人，但和他一起工作的人却看到了他不同的一面。
column14: She is known as an expert in the field. [=people consider her an expert]
column15: 她被认为是该领域的专家。

column10:
[+ as] [often used as (be) known as]
used to indicate the name that people know or use for someone or something
column11: 用于表示人们所知道或使用的某人或某事的名称
column12: Her neighbors knew her as Jill Brown, but her real name was Amy Smith.
column13: 她的邻居们都认识她叫吉尔·布朗，但她的真实名字是艾米·史密斯。
column14: Samuel L. Clemens was better/otherwise known as Mark Twain. [=most people called him Mark Twain]
column15: 塞缪尔·L·克莱门斯更广为人知的名字是马克·吐温。
column16: Beethoven's Third Symphony is widely known as the “Eroica.”
column17: 贝多芬的第三交响曲广为人知，被称为“英雄”。

column10:
[+ for] [usually used as (be) known for]
used to say that someone or something has a particular quality, feature, ability, etc., that people know about
column11: 用来表示某人或某物具有人们所熟知的某种特质、特点、能力等。
column12: Fans of the blues know the city for its live blues clubs.
column13: 蓝调乐迷们因这座城市的现场蓝调俱乐部而闻名。
column14: The restaurant is known for its desserts. [=the restaurant's desserts are popular, well-known, etc.]
column15: 这家餐厅以其甜点闻名。
column16: She is known for her ability to work quickly. = She is known for working quickly.
column17: 她以工作迅速而闻名。
column18: He's known for being late. [=he is often late]
column19: 他以迟到著称。

column10: [Someone who has been known to be or known to do something has been or done that thing in the past.]
column11: 已知某人是某种人或做过某事，表示此人在过去确实是那种人或做过那件事。
column12: We've known him to work all night to meet a deadline. = He's been known to work all night to meet a deadline.
column13: 我们知道他曾经通宵工作以赶上最后期限。
column14: I've never known her to be wrong. [=I do not know of any time when she has been wrong]
column15: 我从未见她犯过错。
column16: He's been known to do this kind of thing before.
column17: 他以前就做过这种事。

column10: used to say that something is expected to happen in the future
column11: 用来说某事预计将在未来发生
column12: We will [=we are going to] leave tomorrow.
column13: 我们明天就要离开。
column14: I will be there in fifteen minutes.
column15: 我十五分钟后到。
column16: Tomorrow will be partly cloudy and cool.
column17: 明天将是多云且凉爽。
column18:
What do you think will happen?
Who do you think will win?
He will be severely punished for this crime.
We will continue our efforts, and we will succeed. [=we are determined to succeed]
column19:
你认为会发生什么？
你认为谁会赢？
他会因为这项罪行而受到严厉的惩罚。
我们会继续努力，并且我们会成功。

column10: used to say that you want something
column11: 用来表示你想要某样东西
column12: I will [=(more commonly) I'll] have a hamburger and fries.
column13: 我会要一个汉堡和薯条。
column14: “Will you have another cup of tea?” “Yes, I will, thank you.”
column15: “你还要再来一杯茶吗？” “好的，谢谢。”

column10: used to say that you are willing to do something
column11: 用来说你愿意做某事
column12: Yes, I will marry you.
column13: 是的，我愿意嫁给你。
column14: The doctor will see you now.
column15: 医生现在会见你。
column16: “Will you help him?” “No, I most certainly will not!”
column17: “你会帮他吗？”“不会，我绝对不会！”
column18: No one would do it.
column19: 没人会这么做。

column10: used to ask someone to do something
column11: 用来请求某人做某事
column12: Will [=would] you please pass the salt?
column13: 请你把盐递给我好吗？
column14: Will you help me with my homework?
column15: 你能帮我做作业吗？
column16: Will you please stop talking?
column17: 你能不能请你别说话了？
column18:
Shut the window, will you?
If you will follow me, ladies and gentlemen, I'll take you to the next gallery.
column19:
请把窗户关上，好吗？
各位女士们先生们，请跟我来，我带大家去下一个展厅。

column10: used to give a command or to say what must happen or not happen
column11: 用于下达命令或说明必须发生或不允许发生的事情
column12: You will do as I say.
column13: 你会按照我说的去做。
column14: Everyone will leave immediately!
column15: 所有人必须立即离开！
column16: I will not have my own children talking to me like that!
column17: 我绝不会让自己的孩子那样跟我说话！
column18: No one will leave this room until a decision has been made.
column19: 在做出决定之前，任何人都不能离开这个房间。

column10: used to say that something is likely or certain to be true
column11: 用来说某事很可能或肯定是真的
column12: That will be the babysitter at the door.
column13: 那应该是保姆在门口。
column14: The gray house on the left will be theirs. [=must be theirs]
column15: 左边的那座灰色房子一定是他们的。
column16: Try this soup—you will like it. [=(more commonly) you'll like it]
column17: 试试这个汤——你会喜欢的。
column18: Ask anyone and they will tell you the same thing.
column19: 问问任何人，他们都会告诉你同样的事情。

column10: used to describe a situation that is continuing
column11: 用来描述正在持续的情况
column12: He won't stop bothering me. [=he keeps bothering me; he refuses to stop bothering me]
column13: 他不停地烦我。
column14: The door won't open.
column15: 门打不开。

column10: used to say that something usually happens or that a person or thing usually does something
column11: 用来表示某事通常会发生，或者某人或某物通常会做某事。
column12: The dog will growl if you get too close to it.
column13: 如果你靠它太近，那只狗会咆哮。
column14: She will wait until the last minute to finish her homework.
column15: 她会等到最后一刻才完成作业。
column16: People will talk if they see us together.
column17: 如果人们看到我们在一起，他们会议论的。
column18:
Accidents will happen. [=accidents sometimes happens; it isn't possible to avoid all accidents]
[In British English, this sense is sometimes used to show that you are annoyed that someone does something often.] He will leave his coat on the chair instead of hanging it up.
column19:
意外总会发生。
他总是把外套放在椅子上，而不是挂起来。

column10: used to say that something is able to do something or contain a certain amount
column11: 用来说某物能够做某事或容纳一定数量。
column12: The batteries will last a maximum of four hours.
column13: 电池最多可持续四个小时。
column14: The back seat will [=can] hold three people. [=it is capable of holding three people]
column15: 后座可以坐三个人。
column16: This will do if there is nothing better.
column17: 如果没有更好的，这个就行。

column10:
[This verb is only used in the simple present tense.]
to want or desire (something)
column11: 想要或渴望（某物）
column12: You can say what you will [=you can say whatever you want to say], but I will always love her.
column13: 你想说什么都可以，但我会一直爱她。
column14: Call it what you will, it is still illegal. [=it is illegal no matter what you call it]
column15: 不管你怎么称呼它，它仍然是非法的。
column16: Imagine, if you will, life without computers.
column17: 请想象一下，没有计算机的生活。
column18: Baseball is my love, my obsession if you will. [=if you want to call it that]
column19: 棒球是我的挚爱，如果你愿意的话，也可以说是我的痴迷。

column10: to cause or try to cause (something) to happen by using the power of your mind
column11: 用你的意念使（某事）发生或试图使其发生
column12: She was haunted by the thought that she had willed his death. [=that she had caused his death by wishing that he would die]
column13: 她一直被这样一个想法困扰：她是因为自己的意愿导致了他的死亡。

column10: to cause or try to cause (someone or something) to do something by using the power of your mind
column11: 用你的意念让（某人或某物）做某事，或试图让其做某事
column12: He willed himself to stay awake.
column13: 他强迫自己保持清醒。
column14: As she neared the finish line she willed her legs to keep running.
column15: 当她接近终点线时，她强迫自己的双腿继续奔跑。

column10: to want or intend (something) to happen
column11: 想要或打算（某事）发生
column12: It will happen if God wills it.
column13: 如果上帝愿意，这将会发生。

column10: to state in a will that (your property) will be given to a particular person, organization, etc., after you die
column11: 在遗嘱中声明（你的财产）将在你去世后被赠予某个特定的人、组织等。
column12: She willed her property to her children.

column16: Who do you think you are, barging in here like that?
column17: 你以为你是谁，竟然这样闯进来？

column10: at or during the time that
column11: 在……的时候

column13: 我们在度假时去钓鱼了。
column14: I'll leave when you do. [=I'll leave at the same time as you]
column15: 你什么时候走，我就什么时候走。
column16: When he finally showed up, he was drunk.
column17: 当他终于出现时，他喝醉了。
column18: When I was in school, we didn't have computers.
column19: 当我上学的时候，我们没有电脑。

column13: 铃响时你可以走了。
column14: Call me when you get home.
column15: 你到家后给我打个电话。
column16: Things were better when he got a job.
column17: 当他找到工作后，情况变得更好了。

column10: at any or every time that
column11: 在任何时候或每当

column13: 每当我听到那首歌时，我都会哭。
column14: When he watches television, he falls asleep.
column15: 当他看电视时，他会睡着。

column10: used to say what happens, is true, or can be done in a particular situation
column11: 用于说明在特定情况下会发生什么、是真的，或可以做什么
column12: When you have no family, you are really on your own.
column13: 当你没有家人时，你真的只能靠自己。
column14: We take the bus to school when it rains.
column15: 下雨的时候我们乘公交车去学校。
column16: A contestant is disqualified when she disobeys the rules.
column17: 当参赛者违反规则时，她会被取消资格。
column18: When and if he comes, you can ask him. = If and when he comes, you can ask him.
column19: 当他来的时候，你可以问他。

column10: used to ask why or how something is done in the situation that exists
column11: 用于询问在现有情况下，为什么或如何做某事
column12: Why buy a newspaper when you can read the news online for free?
column13: 既然你可以免费在网上阅读新闻，为什么还要买报纸？
column14: How can he buy the house when he has no money? [=he has no money, so how can he buy the house?]
column15: 他没有钱，怎么能买房子呢？

column10: in spite of the fact that although
column11: 尽管事实上虽然

column13: 她在本可以拥有辉煌政治生涯的时候却退出了政坛。

column13: 明天是我们必须做出决定的时候。

column10:
[used to indicate what is being shown, pointed to, or mentioned]
what one or ones of a group what particular one or ones
column11: 哪一个或哪些（属于某一组） 哪一个或哪些特定的

column13: 他知道哪些人已经付过钱，哪些人还没有。
column14: Which tie should I wear, the red one or the green one?
column15: 我应该戴哪条领带，红色的还是绿色的？
column16: Which way should we turn at the stoplight?
column17: 在红绿灯处我们应该往哪边转？
column18: Choose which style you like best.
column19: 选择你最喜欢的风格。

column10:
[used to indicate or ask what is being shown, pointed to, or mentioned]
what one or ones out of a group
column11: 哪一个或哪一些（在一组中）

column13: 他们要么在游泳，要么在划独木舟，我不知道是哪一个。
column14: They could not decide which of the two roads to take.
column15: 他们无法决定走哪一条路。
column16: Which of those houses do you live in?
column17: 你住在那些房子中的哪一栋？
column18: Which of you want tea and which want lemonade?
column19: 你们中谁要茶，谁要柠檬水？

column10: used to introduce an additional statement about something that has already been mentioned
column11: 用于引入关于已经提到的事情的补充说明
column12: She plays squash, which is a sport similar to racquetball.
column13: 她打壁球，这是一项类似于短柄墙球的运动。
column14: Our new car, which we bought last month, seats five people.
column15: 我们上个月买的新车可以坐五个人。

column10: used after a preposition to refer again to something that has already been mentioned
column11: 在介词后使用，用来再次指代已经提到过的事物

column14: The exhibit is on view here for three months, after which it travels to another city.
column15: 该展览将在这里展出三个月，之后将移至另一个城市。

column10: used to introduce a group of words that limits the meaning of a noun to a specific place or thing
column11: 用于引入一组限定名词含义为特定地点或事物的词语。
column12: This is a matter which [=that] requires further study.
column13: 这是一个需要进一步研究的问题。

column11: 用于指代某些人、动物或事物，作为动词或介词的宾语。

column13: 他们的母亲开车送他们去参加足球训练。
column14: I haven't met them yet.
column15: 我还没有见过他们。
column16: You can ask any of them for help.
column17: 你可以向他们中的任何一个寻求帮助。
column18: I played basketball with them yesterday.
column19: 我昨天和他们一起打了篮球。

column10:
[used to refer to a single person whose sex is not known or specified]
him or her
column11: 用于指代性别不明或未指明的单个人：他或她

column13: 老师说，如果有人站出来承认恶作剧，她就不会惩罚他或她。

column10:

those

column13: 这可是挑衅的话。

column11: 用于指代未知、未被命名或未被具体说明的人或事物

column13: 你不在的时候有个人打电话来了。
column14: She works for some company (or other/another) out west.
column15: 她在西部为某家公司（或其他/另一家）工作。
column16: For some reason, the lights went out.
column17: 出于某种原因，灯灭了。

Could you call back some other time? I'm busy right now.

I like some kinds of nuts but not all of them.

我试图为这份帮忙给他某种报酬。
你能换个时间再打来吗？我现在很忙。
有些鸟不会飞。
我喜欢某些种类的坚果，但不是所有的都喜欢。
有些人相信这个，而其他人则不信。

column10: of an unspecified amount or number
column11: 数量或数目不详
column12: Can I have some water?
column13: 我可以要点水吗？
column14: I bought some apples.
column15: 我买了一些苹果。
column16: She had some interest in the job.
column17: 她对这份工作有一些兴趣。
column18:
I have some money left, but not much.
I hope I've been of some help.
column19:
我还剩下一些钱，但不多。
希望我能帮上一点忙。

column10: of a fairly large amount or number
column11: 相当大量或数量的

column13: 他们的决定引起了相当大的惊讶。

column15: 她要过一段时间才会回来。

column17: 我们几年前见过面。

column19: 他详细谈论了他的问题。

column11: 用来表示赞同

column13: 那真是一场精彩的比赛！

column13: 你真有胆量竟然说那种话！

column15: 你不知道怎么去那里？你还说自己是导航员呢！

column17: 他算什么朋友——把我一个人扔在火车站不管了。

column10: an unspecified amount or number of people or things
column11: 未指明数量的人或物

column19:
这家面包店做的面包是镇上最好的之一。
我正在煮咖啡，你要来一杯吗？
有些人说耐心是一种美德。

column10: having a specified quality

column10: causing a specified feeling or condition

column16: quarrelsome
column17: 好争吵的

column10:
[usually + from]
to borrow or use (a phrase, an idea, etc., that was created by a different person or used in a different place)
column11: 借用或使用（由他人创造或在其他地方使用的短语、想法等）
column12: a quotation taken from Shakespeare
column13: 摘自莎士比亚的一句话
column14: The album's title is taken from [=it is the same as] a line in the album's first song.
column15: 这张专辑的标题取自专辑第一首歌中的一句歌词。
column16: The builders took their inspiration from [=the builders were inspired by] the Acropolis in Athens.
column17: 建筑者们的灵感来自雅典的卫城。

column10: to begin to have (a particular shape or form)
column11: 开始具有（特定的形状或形式）
column12: The college took its present form after World War II.
column13: 这所学院在二战后形成了现在的样貌。
column14: The plan is finally starting to take form/shape. [=to have a definite arrangement]
column15: 这个计划终于开始成形了。

column10: to choose to have (something)
column11: 选择拥有（某物）
column12: He'll have the fish and I'll take the chicken.
column13: 他要鱼，我要鸡。
column14: Do you take cream in your coffee?
column15: 你的咖啡里加奶油吗？
column16: You can have either one. Take your pick. [=choose whichever one you want]
column17: 你可以任选一个。随便挑吧。

column10: to accept or receive (something) as payment or as a response
column11: 接受或接收（某物）作为付款或回应
column12: Do you take credit cards?
column13: 你们接受信用卡吗？
column14: an elected official accused of taking bribes
column15: 一名被指控收受贿赂的民选官员
column16: (Brit) The restaurant took [=(US) took in] an enormous amount of money in its first week of business.
column17: （英）这家餐厅在开业的第一周赚了大量的钱。
column18:
I was hoping they would pay me more, but at this point I'll take what I can get.
I insist that you come to my party, and I won't take no for an answer!
column19:
我本来希望他们能多付点钱，但现在我能拿到什么就拿什么了。
我坚持要你来参加我的派对，我不会接受你的拒绝！

column10: to accept (something, such as blame, credit, or responsibility)
column11: 接受（某事，例如责备、表扬或责任）
column12: I take full responsibility for what happened.
column13: 我对所发生的事情负全部责任。
column14: No one else was willing to take the blame/rap (for what happened).
column15: 没有其他人愿意为（所发生的事情）承担责任/背黑锅。
column16: I did the work and he took all the credit.
column17: 我做了所有的工作，而他却把所有的功劳都归于自己。

column10: to allow (someone) to join a club, to attend a school, to become part of a relationship, etc.
column11: 允许（某人）加入俱乐部、就读学校、成为某种关系的一部分等。
column12: The school takes [=admits] just 20 students a year.
column13: 这所学校每年只招收20名学生。
column14: The doctor's office is not taking [=accepting] any new patients.
column15: 医生诊所目前不接受新病人。
column16: (old-fashioned) It is time for you to take a wife/husband. [=to get married]
column17: （老式用法）你该娶妻/嫁人了。

column10: to be able to hold (a number of people or things) to have enough room for (something)
column11: 能够容纳（一定数量的人或物）；有足够的空间容放（某物）
column12: I think the elevator will take a few more people.
column13: 我认为电梯还能再容纳几个人。

column10: to need or require (something)
column11: 需要（某物）
column12: What size shoe do you take?
column13: 你穿多大码的鞋？
column14: It took four people to move the couch.
column15: 搬这张沙发花了四个人的力气。
column16: What would it take to get you to buy this car?
column17: 要让你买下这辆车，需要什么条件？
column18:
It will take several years to finish the bridge. = The bridge will take several years to finish.
Do you have what it takes [=do you have the skills and personality] to do this job?
The new color is nice, but it'll take some getting used to. [=I will need to get used to it]
Be patient. These things take (a lot of) time. [=a lot of time needs to pass before they happen or are finished]
Keeping everyone happy does take a lot of doing. = It takes some doing. [=it requires a lot of work]
column19:
建造这座桥需要好几年时间。
你有能力胜任这份工作吗？
新颜色挺好看的，但需要一段时间来适应。
要有耐心。这些事情需要（很多）时间。
让每个人都满意确实很难做到。

column10: [The phrases it takes two and it takes two to tango are used to say that two people or groups are needed in order to do something.]
column11: 短语 it takes two 和 it takes two to tango 用来表示做某事需要两个人或两个团体。
column12: Both of you should be punished for fighting. It takes two, you know.
column13: 你们俩都应该因为打架而受到惩罚。你们要知道，打架是两个人的事。
column14: We'd like to continue negotiating, but it takes two to tango—we can't solve this problem by ourselves.
column15: 我们希望继续谈判，但一个巴掌拍不响——我们无法单独解决这个问题。

column10: to do or perform (something)
column11: 去做或执行（某事）
column12: Let's take a walk. [=let's walk]
column13: 我们去散步吧。
column14: He's taking a shower [=he's showering] upstairs.
column15: 他正在楼上洗澡。
column16: Take a look/peek/gander at this.
column17: 看看这个。
column18:
How old do you think I am? Take a guess.
The kids take their naps around one o'clock.
He took a bite of his sandwich.
Take a deep breath and try to calm down.
We are taking a tour of the building tomorrow.
They took a pledge never to tell anyone their secret.
It's time for you to take a stand [=to express your opinion] and tell them that things need to change.
column19:
你觉得我几岁？猜猜看。
孩子们大约在一点钟午睡。
他咬了一口三明治。
深呼吸，试着冷静下来。
我们明天要参观这栋楼。
他们发誓永远不把他们的秘密告诉任何人。
现在是你表明立场并告诉他们事情需要改变的时候了。

column10: to get (a drug, pill, etc.) into your body by swallowing it, breathing it in, etc.
column11: 通过吞咽、吸入等方式将（药物、药丸等）摄入体内。
column12: Take one of these pills in the morning and one before bedtime.
column13: 早上服用一片这些药丸，睡前再服用一片。
column14: She refuses to take her medicine.
column15: 她拒绝吃她的药。
column16: She stopped taking drugs [=she stopped using illegal drugs] years ago.
column17: 她多年前就戒掉了毒品。

column10: to sit or stand in (a particular place) to move into position on (a stage, field, etc.)
column11: 坐在或站在（某个特定的地方）；移动到（舞台、场地等）的位置上。
column12: Please take a seat. [=please sit down]
column13: 请坐。
column14: I took my place next to her at the table.
column15: 我在桌子旁坐到她旁边。
column16: The actors took their places on the stage.
column17: 演员们在舞台上各就各位。
column18:
They took the stage for their final bow.
The home team is now taking the field.
Will the next witness please take the stand?
She took the witness stand.
The senator from Nevada would now like to take the floor. [=to begin speaking at a public meeting]
column19:
他们登上舞台，进行最后的谢幕。
主队现在正在上场。
请下一位证人上证人席。
她走上了证人席。
来自内华达州的参议员现在想要发言。

column10: to create or record (a picture or image)
column11: 创作或记录（一幅图片或图像）
column12: She took our picture in front of the waterfall.
column13: 她在瀑布前给我们拍了照。
column14: Our new camera takes beautiful pictures.
column15: 我们的新相机拍出来的照片非常漂亮。
column16: The doctor wants to take an X-ray of your leg.
column17: 医生想给你的腿拍一张X光片。
column18: They arrested him and took his fingerprints.
column19: 他们逮捕了他，并采集了他的指纹。

column10: to find out (a person's temperature, height, etc.)
column11: 测量（某人的体温、身高等）
column12: The last time we took his temperature, it was 102 degrees.
column13: 上次我们给他量体温时，是102度。
column14: The nurse weighed me and took my blood pressure.
column15: 护士给我称了体重，并测量了我的血压。
column16: Before the seamstress can make your dress, she has to take your measurements.
column17: 在裁缝为你制作裙子之前，她必须先为你量尺寸。

column10: to find out and write down (information)
column11: 查明并写下（信息）
column12: He took my name and number and said he would call me back.
column13: 他记下了我的名字和电话号码，说会回电给我。

column10: to create (a list or a record of information)
column11: 创建（一个列表或一份信息记录）
column12: I can't come to class today. Would you mind taking notes for me?
column13: 我今天不能来上课。你介意帮我记笔记吗？
column14: The census we took last year shows that our population is growing very rapidly.
column15: 我们去年进行的人口普查显示，我们的人口正在迅速增长。
column16: We took an inventory at the store yesterday to find out what we need to order.
column17: 我们昨天在商店进行了盘点，以确定我们需要订购什么。

column10: to travel using (a road, vehicle, etc.)
column11: 使用（道路、交通工具等）旅行
column12: We took the highway into the city.
column13: 我们开车走高速公路进了城。
column14: She had to take a different route home.
column15: 她不得不走一条不同的路回家。
column16: He takes the subway to work.
column17: 他乘地铁去上班。

column10: to turn toward (a particular direction)
column11: 转向（特定方向）
column12: Take a right [=turn right] at the next stop light.
column13: 在下一个红绿灯处向右转。
column14: Take your first left and go straight for a mile.
column15: 在第一个路口向左转，然后直行一英里。
column16: We took a wrong turn [=went the wrong way; turned in the wrong direction] and got lost.
column17: 我们拐错了弯，结果迷路了。

column10: to move on or over (something) in a particular way
column11: 以特定的方式在（某物）上移动或越过
column12: He took the stairs [=went up/down the stairs] two at a time.
column13: 他一次跨两级台阶上下楼梯。
column14: She took the curve too fast and the car skidded.
column15: 她过弯太快，汽车打滑了。

column10: to agree to do or have (a job, role, etc.)
column11: 同意做或担任（某项工作、角色等）
column12: He took a job as a janitor at the high school.
column13: 他在高中找了一份清洁工的工作。
column14: She hasn't decided if she is going to take the position or not.
column15: 她还没有决定是否要接受这个职位。
column16: I took a few overtime shifts this month.
column17: 这个月我加了几次班。
column18:
He took the role of Romeo in the play.
She says that parents should be taking a more active role in their children's education. [=should be more actively involved in their children's education]
The former governor took office [=became governor] in 1998.
She was the first woman to take her seat [=to begin her official duties as a member] in Parliament.
column19:
他在这部戏中扮演了罗密欧的角色。
她说父母应该在孩子的教育中扮演更积极的角色。
前州长于1998年上任。
她是第一位在议会就职的女性。

column10: to teach (a person or class) or lead (a religious service)
column11: 教授（某人或班级）或主持（宗教仪式）
column12: The new teacher took us for English.
column13: 新老师给我们上了英语课。
column14: She took a class of eight children.
column15: 她带了一个有八个孩子的班级。
column16: The vicar won't be able to take the early service.
column17: 牧师将无法主持早晨的礼拜。

column10: to study (a subject) or participate in (a class) as a student
column11: 作为学生学习（某一学科）或参加（某一课程）
column12: Her parents made her take piano lessons when she was 10.
column13: 她父母在她10岁时让她学钢琴。
column14: He takes both French and Spanish.
column15: 他同时学习法语和西班牙语。
column16: I took five classes last semester.
column17: 我上个学期上了五门课。
column18: I'm taking a course on world history.
column19: 我正在上一门世界历史课程。

column10: to complete (a test or exam)
column11: 完成（测试或考试）
column12: If you fail the first time, you have to take the test again.
column13: 如果你第一次没通过，你必须再次参加考试。

column10: to use or need (something) in order to work
column11: 使用或需要（某物）才能工作
column12: What size batteries does the flashlight take?
column13: 手电筒使用什么型号的电池？
column14: a car that takes diesel
column15: 一辆使用柴油的汽车

column10: to use (something) for a particular purpose
column11: 将（某物）用于特定目的
column12: The team's coaches decided to take another approach.
column13: 球队的教练们决定采取另一种方法。
column14: Let me take this opportunity to thank everyone for coming.
column15: 让我借此机会感谢大家的到来。
column16: Harsh measures were taken to reduce crime in the city.
column17: 为了减少城市犯罪，采取了严厉的措施。
column18:
I suggest you take his advice.
They never took the time [=bothered] to get to know her.
column19:
我建议你采纳他的建议。
他们从未花时间去了解她。

column10: to accept (the power to deal with something) to accept control of (something)
column11: 接受（处理某事的能力）；接受对（某事）的控制
column12: She was chosen to take charge/control of the organization.
column13: 她被选中负责管理该组织。
column14: I'll get you started, and you take it [=take over] from there.
column15: 我会帮你起个头，然后你接着来。
column16: Citizens are discouraged from taking the law into their own hands. [=punishing people for breaking laws even though they have no right to punish them]
column17: 不鼓励公民私自执法。

column10: to make (a decision) with authority
column11: 以权威作出（决定）
column12: The committee will take [=make] their decision next week.
column13: 委员会将在下周做出他们的决定。

column10: to deal with or consider (something)
column11: 处理或考虑（某事）
column12: The governor will give a statement and then take questions from reporters.
column13: 州长将发表声明，然后接受记者提问。
column14: Will you take this call?
column15: 你会接这个电话吗？
column16: Cases will be taken in order of importance.
column17: 案件将按照重要性顺序处理。
column18:
Let's take first things first.
We'll see what happens and take it as it comes.
I'll need a long time to recover, so I'm just taking (it) one day at a time.
column19:
让我们先把最重要的事情处理好。
我们走一步看一步，顺其自然。
我需要很长时间来恢复，所以我只能一天一天慢慢来。

column10: to understand or think about (something or someone) in a certain way
column11: 以某种方式理解或看待（某事或某人）
column12: I don't quite know how to take that comment.
column13: 我不太知道该如何理解那句话。
column14: He said that I was full-figured, and I took it as a compliment.
column15: 他说我身材丰满，我把这当作是一种赞美。
column16: No one took her literally/seriously when she said that she was going to quit.
column17: 当她说她要辞职时，没有人把她的话当真。
column18:
He takes himself too seriously.
He says unkind things to everyone. Try not to take it personally. [=to be offended or upset by what he said]
Don't take this the wrong way [=do not be offended by this], but I think you could find a better boyfriend.
When it started to rain, we took it as a sign [=we believed that the rain was a sign] that we should go home.
Can't you take a hint? [=understand that I am trying to give you a hint?]
I take it [=(more formally) assume, suppose] that you didn't get my message.
So, you're staying here, I take it.
I know it's just gossip, so I take it for what it's worth. [=I do not strongly believe that it is true or important]
column19:
他太把自己当回事了。
他对每个人都说些不友善的话。尽量不要往心里去。
别误会我的意思，但我觉得你可以找到更好的男朋友。
当开始下雨时，我们把这当作一个信号，觉得我们应该回家了。
你就不能领会一下吗？
我猜你没收到我的消息。
所以，你要留在这里，对吧？
我知道这只是八卦，所以我不会太当真。

column10: to react to (someone or something) in a certain way
column11: 以某种方式对（某人或某事）作出反应
column12: I was surprised by how well she took the news.
column13: 她对这个消息的反应之好让我感到惊讶。
column14: He took it pretty badly/hard [=he was very upset] when his dog died.
column15: 当他的狗去世时，他非常难过/伤心。
column16: She doesn't take such things lightly. [=she acts as though such things are very important]
column17: 她不会对这种事情掉以轻心。

column10: to think about (something or someone) as an example
column11: 把（某事或某人）作为一个例子来思考
column12: They just want attention. For instance, take the way they wear their hair.
column13: 他们只是想引起注意。例如，看看他们梳头发的方式。
column14: Take last year's record high temperatures, for example.
column15: 以去年的创纪录高温为例。
column16: The system isn't working properly. Take the case of Jane Smith.
column17: 系统运行不正常。以简·史密斯为例。

column10:
[usually + for]
to think of (someone or something) as a particular type of person or thing
column11: 把（某人或某事）看作是某种类型的人或事物
column12: Oh, you're not Jill. Excuse me. I took you for [=mistakenly thought you were] an old friend of mine.
column13: 哦，你不是吉尔。对不起。我把你当成了我的一位老朋友。
column14: Of course we know how to do it. Do you take us for idiots? [=do you think we are idiots?]
column15: 我们当然知道怎么做。你把我们当傻子吗？
column16: “Can you finish everything in two hours?” “Two hours?! Who do you take me for? Superman?” [=do you think I'm Superman?]
column17: “你能在两个小时内完成所有事情吗？” “两个小时？！你把我当成谁了？超人吗？”

column10: to believe (something that someone tells you)
column11: 相信（某人告诉你的事情）
column12: Take it from me. [=believe me] He would love to go to the concert with you.
column13: 相信我。他很想和你一起去听音乐会。
column14: Okay, I'll take your word for it. [=I will believe that what you say is true]
column15: 好的，我就相信你说的话。
column16: You don't have to take my word for it. Ask him yourself.
column17: 你不必只听我的话。你可以自己去问他。
column18: She can't take a compliment. [=she does not believe that the nice things said about her are true]
column19: 她无法接受表扬。

column10: to begin to have (an opinion, interest, etc.)
column11: 开始产生（观点、兴趣等）
column12: She has yet to take a position on the issue.
column13: 她尚未就该问题表明立场。
column14: The program inspires young people to take an interest [=become interested] in current events.
column15: 该项目激励年轻人对时事产生兴趣。
column16: They take a dim view [=have a negative opinion] of the country's current foreign policy.
column17: 他们对该国当前的外交政策持负面看法。
column18: She took a dim view of his behavior.
column19: 她对他的行为持否定态度。

column10: to ask people to make choices or give opinions in (a vote, poll, etc.)
column11: 要求人们在（投票、民意调查等）中做出选择或发表意见
column12: They took a survey of shoppers to find out which brands people liked best.
column13: 他们对购物者进行了调查，以了解人们最喜欢哪些品牌。
column14: I think we should take a vote [=should vote] about what to do.
column15: 我认为我们应该投票决定该怎么做。

column10:
[often + in or to]
to feel or experience (an emotion)
column11: 感受或经历（一种情感）
column12: Please don't take offense. [=please don't be offended]
column13: 请不要生气。
column14: Investors took fright [=suddenly became afraid] at the news and pulled their money.
column15: 投资者因这则消息受惊，于是撤回了他们的资金。
column16: His grandparents took special pleasure in [=were very pleased by] seeing him graduate from college.
column17: 他的祖父母看到他大学毕业感到格外高兴。
column18:
It's important to take pride in your work.
I take comfort/solace in the fact that others have had to go through the same thing.
She takes an instant dislike to [=she instantly dislikes] anyone who tries to sell her something.
column19:
为自己的工作感到自豪是很重要的。
我感到安慰的是，其他人也经历过同样的事情。
她对任何试图向她推销东西的人都会立刻产生反感。

column10: [If you are taken ill/sick or (US) take ill/sick, you suddenly become ill.]
column11: 突然生病
column12: He and I both took ill after eating the fish.
column13: 我和他在吃了那条鱼后都生病了。
column14: Several other customers also were taken ill/sick.
column15: 还有其他几位顾客也生病了。

column10: to experience or be affected by (something unpleasant)
column11: 经历或受到（某些不愉快的事情）的影响
column12: Everyone will have to take a pay cut.
column13: 每个人都将不得不接受减薪。
column14: She had to take a two-stroke penalty.
column15: 她不得不接受两杆罚杆。
column16: The ship sunk after taking [=sustaining] a direct hit.
column17: 这艘船在遭受直接打击后沉没了。
column18:
He took several punches to the head.
He took quite a beating.
“Take that,” she said as she slapped him in the face.
column19:

column15: 我正好赶到，看到他获胜。

我们到那儿大概只需要不到/超过一个小时。

column18: The restaurant is just around the corner.
column19: 餐厅就在拐角处。

“Who is she?” “Oh, just somebody who works in the same office as me.”

They took a nice field and turned it into just another shopping mall.

column19:
我到哪里都能看到他，这只是巧合吗？

他不过是又一个想不怎么努力就发财的家伙。

column10: used to stress the simple truth of a description or statement
column11: 用于强调描述或陈述的简单事实

column15: 有时候，一个人只是想要被独处。

column17: 她只是想说再见。

The wedding was just wonderful.
I feel just great!

婚礼真是太美好了。

column15: 女士们，先生们，请这边走。

column11: 用于强调你下达命令或提出建议时

column13: 我们干脆把这件事全都忘了吧。

column15: 等一下！你刚才说你已经解决了这个问题？!

Just think how happy we could be.
column19:

别跟我争辩：照做就是了！
想象一下，当她意识到自己错了时，会觉得多尴尬。
你看看那东西有多大！
想想我们能有多幸福。

column10: used to describe what someone does instead of doing what is necessary or expected

column13: 别光站在那里，做点什么吧！

column15: 她只是站在那里，看着他离开。
column16: I can't just pretend nothing happened.
column17: 我不能就这样假装什么都没发生。

column10: used with words like might and may to refer to something that is possible

column13: 我知道你并不指望他会成功，但他也许会让你大吃一惊。

column16: You know, you just might be right about that.
column17: 你知道吗，你说的也许是对的。

I saw her take the money.
Nobody saw the accident happen.

It was so dark that I couldn't see.

I can't see over the person in front of me.

column19: 这个决定让他很不舒服。

column10: in a kind, friendly, or generous way
column11: 以一种友善、亲切或慷慨的方式
column12: The novel was well received by the critics.
column13: 这部小说受到了评论家的好评。
column14: They always speak well of you.
column15: 他们总是说你的好话。
column16: I wish her well. [=I hope she does well; I hope that she succeeds]
column17: 我祝她一切顺利。
column18:
He means well [=he has good intentions], but he's not really helping anyone.
The company did well by me when I retired. [=the company treated me well when I retired]
column19:
他是出于好意，但实际上并没有真正帮到任何人。
我退休时，公司对我很好。

column10: completely or fully
column11: 完全地或彻底地
column12: We are well aware of the problem.
column13: 我们非常清楚这个问题。
column14: The food at the restaurant is well worth the trip.
column15: 这家餐厅的食物非常值得专程前往。
column16: Their kitchen is well equipped.
column17: 他们的厨房设备齐全。
column18:
Your promotion is well deserved.
The plane was well out of sight.
I can understand your dilemma very well.
She knows the area quite well.
I knew him well when we were in high school together.
I remember her well enough. = I remember her fairly well.
column19:
你的晋升实至名归。
飞机早已飞出视线。
我非常能理解你的困境。
她对这个地区非常熟悉。
我们上高中时我和他很熟。
我对她还有些印象。

column10: to a great degree or extent
column11: 在很大程度上
column12: The group has sold well over a million albums.
column13: 该乐队的专辑销量已远超一百万张。
column14: The temperature will be well [=far] above average today. It will be well into the nineties.
column15: 今天的气温将远高于平均水平。气温将达到九十多华氏度。
column16: He is well on his way to becoming a superstar.
column17: 他正在顺利地走向成为超级明星的道路上。
column18:
I'm well into the book and should finish it soon.
She walked well ahead of the group.
column19:
我已经读了这本书的大部分，很快就能读完。
她走在队伍的前面很远。

column10:
[usually used with can, could, may, or might]
used for emphasis to say that something is or is not proper, appropriate, etc.
column11: 用于强调某事是否合适、得当等。
column12: She's angry, and well she should be. [=she has a good reason to be angry]
column13: 她很生气，而且她确实应该生气。
column14: I cannot very well refuse the invitation. [=it would be improper for me to refuse the invitation]
column15: 我实在无法拒绝这个邀请。
column16: I couldn't very well just walk right in!
column17: 我可不能就这么直接走进去！
column18:
And what, one might/may well ask, makes this computer system worth its high price?
The decision may well be questioned.
column19:
那么，人们很可能会问，这台计算机系统凭什么值这么高的价格？
这个决定很可能会受到质疑。

column10:
[usually used with could, may, or might]
very possibly
column11: 很有可能
column12: You could very well be right. [=it is very possible that you are right]
column13: 你很可能是对的。
column14: The concert may well be sold-out. [=it is possible/likely that the concert is sold-out]
column15: 音乐会很可能已经售罄。
column16: It may well be true.
column17: 这很可能是真的。

column10: without doubt or question
column11: 毫无疑问
column12: They can well afford to be generous.
column13: 他们完全有能力慷慨大方。
column14: As you well know, I don't approve of this. = As you know very well, I don't approve of this.
column15: 正如你非常清楚的那样，我不赞成这件事。
column16: You know perfectly well how to do it.
column17: 你非常清楚该怎么做。
column18: Their relationship is well and truly over.
column19: 他们的关系确实已经彻底结束了。

column10: no more than
column11: 不超过
column12: They lost only [=just, merely] one game this season.
column13: 他们本赛季只输了一场比赛。
column14: I've met him only once. = I've only met him once.
column15: 我只见过他一次。
column16: She had been there only twice in her life.
column17: 她一生中只去过那里两次。
column18:
We have only five minutes to get there. = We only have five minutes to get there.
There are only two more weeks until summer vacation.
It's only a matter of time before someone gets hurt.
Do you really have to leave? It's only eight o'clock.
He was only a baby when his father died.
Leave her alone. She's only a kid.
The building is only about 10 years old.
She plays several instruments including the guitar, violin, and piano, to name only [=but] a few.
It was quiet in the room, but only for a moment.
She is only partly/partially to blame.
column19:
我们只有五分钟到那里。
距离暑假只有两周了。
只是时间问题，迟早会有人受伤。
你真的要走吗？现在才八点。
他父亲去世时，他还只是个婴儿。
别管她了。她只是个孩子。
这栋楼大约只有10年历史。
她会演奏多种乐器，包括吉他、小提琴和钢琴，仅举几例。
房间里很安静，但只持续了一会儿。
她只需承担部分责任。

column10:
[used to indicate that a single thing was done, is needed, is possible, etc.]
nothing other than
column11: 仅仅，只有，除了……之外没有别的
column12: I asked him a question, but he only smiled in response.
column13: 我问了他一个问题，但他只是微笑着回应。
column14: I'm happy to help. You only have/need to ask. = (more formally) You have only to ask. = (more formally) You need only ask. [=I will gladly help you if you ask me to]
column15: 我很乐意帮忙。你只需要开口。
column16: We can only guess/imagine/wonder [=we cannot know] what they will do next.
column17: 我们只能猜测/想象/猜想他们接下来会做什么。
column18: One can only hope for the best. [=there is nothing to do but hope for the best]
column19: 只能寄希望于最好的结果。

column10:
[sometimes used in the phrase only just]
used for emphasis
column11: 用于强调
column12: I only wish [=I wish very much] you'd told me sooner.
column13: 我真希望你早点告诉我。
column14: I only hope that the mistake will be corrected soon.
column15: 我只希望这个错误能尽快得到纠正。
column16: It's only natural [=it's normal/reasonable] (that) you would feel that way.
column17: 你有那样的感觉是很自然的。
column18:
We only just missed the bus. [=we missed it by a very small amount of time; we almost caught the bus]
Our trip had only just begun.
column19:
我们刚刚错过了公交车。
我们的旅程才刚刚开始。

column10: excluding all others; nobody or nothing except
column11: 排除所有其他人；除了……之外没有人或没有任何东西
column12: The club is for women only.
column13: 该俱乐部仅限女性。
column14: The sign on the door says “Employees Only.”
column15: 门上的标牌写着“仅限员工”。
column16: Only employees can use that door.
column17: 只有员工可以使用那扇门。
column18:
I love only you and no one else.
She said only that she knew him. [=she said nothing other than that she knew him]
The storm destroyed the house leaving only a pile of rubble.
That sound can mean only one thing. = That sound can only mean one thing.
Only the strongest will survive.
Only the best fabric will do. [=I want nothing except the best fabric]
The restaurant serves only vegetarian cuisine.
For reasons known only to her/herself, she sold her house and left town.
column19:
我只爱你，不爱其他任何人。
她只说她认识他。
暴风雨摧毁了房子，只剩下一堆瓦砾。
那个声音只能意味着一件事。
只有最强者才能生存。
只有最好的布料才行。
这家餐厅只提供素食。
出于只有她自己知道的原因，她卖掉了房子，离开了小镇。

column10: in no time, place, or situation except the one specified
column11: 除指定的时间、地点或情况外，均不适用
column12: Violence should be used only as a last resort. = Violence should only be used as a last resort.
column13: 暴力应当只作为最后的手段使用。
column14: It should be used only when (it's) absolutely necessary.
column15: 只有在绝对必要时才应使用。
column16: Only then did I realize that I had made a mistake.
column17: 直到那时我才意识到自己犯了一个错误。
column18:
The animal is found only on the continent of Australia.
Only in America can such things happen! [=such things cannot happen anywhere but in America]
The drug is available only by prescription. = The drug is available by prescription only.
I'll go only if he goes with me. = (more strongly) I'll go if and only if he goes with me.
We made the change only after careful consideration of the consequences.
column19:
这种动物只在澳大利亚大陆发现。
只有在美国才会发生这样的事情！
这种药只能凭处方购买。
只有他和我一起去，我才会去。
我们只有在仔细考虑后果之后才做出了改变。

column10: for no other reason than
column11: 仅仅因为没有其他原因
column12: I came here only because she asked me to.
column13: 我来这里只是因为她让我来的。
column14: only for the sake of argument
column15: 只是为了讨论而已

column10: nothing more important or serious than
column11: 没有什么比……更重要或更严重的
column12: It was only [=just, merely] a minor accident. No one got hurt.
column13: 这只是一场小事故。没有人受伤。
column14: I'm fine. It's only a scratch.
column15: 我没事。只是擦伤而已。
column16: “Who was that on the phone?” “Oh, it was only a salesperson.”
column17: “刚才打电话的是谁？”“哦，只是一个推销员。”
column18:
I didn't hit him. I only touched him!
She didn't mean to insult you. She was only joking!
They were only following orders.
column19:
我没有打他。我只是碰了他一下！
她不是故意侮辱你的。她只是开个玩笑！
他们只是执行命令。

column10: used to emphasize that something happened recently
column11: 用来强调某事最近发生了
column12: It happened only [=just] last week.
column13: 这事就发生在上周。
column14: I saw her here only a moment ago.
column15: 我刚才还在这里看到她。
column16: Only in the last few years have we come to understand the condition.
column17: 直到最近几年，我们才开始了解这种状况。
column18: It seems like only yesterday that you were a baby.
column19: 仿佛昨天你还是个婴儿。

column10: used to say that something has or will have a particular and usually bad result
column11: 用来说某事已经或将会产生某种特定且通常是不好的结果
column12: You shouldn't eat that. It will only make you sick.
column13: 你不应该吃那个。那只会让你生病。
column14: The large number of people who came to help only added to the confusion.
column15: 前来帮忙的众多人只会让混乱加剧。

column10:
[followed by to + verb]
used to indicate something bad or surprising that happens after something else
column11: 用于表示在某事之后发生了不好的或令人惊讶的事情。
column12: They won the battle, only to lose the war. [=they won the battle but lost the war]
column13: 他们赢得了战斗，却输了战争。
column14: I ran to the station only to find (that) I had missed the train.
column15: 我跑到车站，却发现我已经错过了火车。

column10:
[often + about] [often + that] [often + what, where, etc.] [This sense of tell is often used informally to emphasize a statement.]
to say or write (something) to (someone)
column11: 对（某人）说或写（某事）
column12: He told us the story.
column13: 他给我们讲了这个故事。
column14: Has she told you the good news, yet?
column15: 她已经告诉你那个好消息了吗？
column16: Please tell us your name and occupation.
column17: 请告诉我们您的姓名和职业。
column18:
She looked at the palm of my hand and told me my fortune.
I promise not to tell anyone your secret. = I promise not to tell your secret to anyone.
You can tell me all about your trip at dinner.
If you see her, tell her (that) we miss her.
People tell me (that) Paris is nice this time of year.
I keep telling myself (that) everything will be OK.
My husband tells/told me (that) you play golf.
He told us what happened.
Can you tell them how to play the game while I get the cards?
I can't tell you how pleased we are [=we are very pleased] that you could join us.
You are wrong, I tell you.
I can tell you —it's not worth the hassle.
I'm telling you, I don't know anyone by that name.
I'll tell you one thing: she was awfully arrogant.
I'll tell you something/this: I would never have bought that car.
Let me tell you (something): he may be old, but he can still win baseball games.
To tell you the truth, I didn't really like the movie.
“The car turned out to be a lemon!” “What did I tell you?” [=you should have listened to me; you should have followed my advice]
column19:
她看着我的手掌，给我算了命。
我保证不会把你的秘密告诉任何人。
你可以在晚餐时把你的旅行经历都告诉我。
如果你见到她，告诉她我们想她了。
人们跟我说巴黎这个季节很美。
我一直在告诉自己一切都会好起来的。
我丈夫跟我说你会打高尔夫。
他告诉了我们发生了什么。
你能在我拿牌的时候告诉他们怎么玩这个游戏吗？
我无法用言语表达我们有多高兴你能加入我们。
你错了，我告诉你。
我可以告诉你——这事不值得费那个劲。
我跟你说，我真的不认识那个名字的人。
我只告诉你一件事：她非常傲慢。
我告诉你一件事：我绝不会买那辆车。
让我告诉你一件事：他虽然年纪大了，但还是能赢棒球比赛。
说实话，我其实不太喜欢那部电影。
“那辆车结果是个破烂货！” “我早就跟你说过了吧？”

column10: to say (a word or words) to (someone)
column11: 对（某人）说（一个词或一些话）

column13: 我没来得及和他说再见。
column14: If you see her, tell her hello for me.
column15: 如果你见到她，替我向她问好。
column16: “I feel sick,” he told his mom.
column17: “我觉得不舒服，”他对妈妈说。

column10: to give information to (someone) by speaking or writing
column11: 通过口头或书面方式向（某人）提供信息
column12: “What is his name?” “I don't know. He didn't tell me.”
column13: “他叫什么名字？”“我不知道。他没告诉我。”
column14: Be sure to tell me when they get here. = When they get here, be sure to tell me (so).
column15: 他们到的时候一定要告诉我。
column16: “I know the answer.” “Don't tell me. [=don't say what the answer is] I want to guess.”
column17: “我知道答案。” “别告诉我。 我想猜一猜。”
column18:
“Do you know where the library is?” “I'm sorry. I couldn't tell you.” [=I don't know]
“Who is the letter from?” “I'm not telling.”
column19:
“你知道图书馆在哪里吗？” “对不起，我不知道。”
“这封信是谁写的？” “我不告诉你。”

column10: to let (someone) know a secret
column11: 让（某人）知道一个秘密
column12: I promise not to tell anyone.
column13: 我保证不会告诉任何人。
column14: I can't tell you because it's a secret.
column15: 我不能告诉你，因为这是个秘密。
column16: Your secret is safe with me: I'll never tell.
column17: 你的秘密在我这里很安全：我绝不会说出去。

column10: to express (something) by speaking
column11: 用口头表达（某事）
column12: He loves telling stories/jokes.
column13: 他喜欢讲故事/笑话。
column14: You shouldn't tell [=reveal] other people's secrets.
column15: 你不应该泄露别人的秘密。
column16: She got in trouble for telling a lie.
column17: 她因为说谎而惹上了麻烦。
column18:
I'm telling the truth.
I didn't really like the movie, to tell the truth. [=to say what I really think]
Truth be told [=to say what the truth is], the food was pretty bad.
column19:
我说的是真的。
说实话，我其实不太喜欢那部电影。
说实话，食物真的很差。

column10:
[usually followed by to + verb]
to give (someone) an instruction or command
column11: 给（某人）下达指示或命令
column12: Be quiet and do what I tell you. = Be quiet and do as you're told.
column13: 安静，照我说的去做。
column14: The police officer told him to stop.
column15: 警察让他停下。
column16: I was told to stay here.
column17: 有人让我待在这里。
column18:
I'll tell them to meet us there at 6 o'clock.
I told myself to pick up some milk on the way home, but I forgot to do it.
You can't tell me what to do.
column19:
我会让他们六点钟在那里和我们见面。
我提醒自己回家的路上要买点牛奶，但我还是忘了。
你不能命令我该做什么。

column10:
[used especially by children]
to inform others that someone has done something wrong or behaved badly
column11: 告知他人某人做错了事或行为不当
column12: If you do that, I'll tell.
column13: 如果你那样做，我就会告诉别人。
column14: I'm telling Mom.
column15: 我要告诉妈妈。

column10: to give information to (someone or something) by doing a particular action or making a particular sound
column11: 通过做某个特定的动作或发出某个特定的声音来向（某人或某物）传递信息
column12: When the dog scratches at the door, she is telling you that she wants to go outside.
column13: 当狗在门上抓挠时，她是在告诉你她想出去。
column14: The oven will beep to tell you when it is preheated.
column15: 烤箱预热完成时会发出蜂鸣声提醒您。

column10: to make (something) known to (someone)
column11: 使（某事）为（某人）所知
column12: The expressions on their faces told me everything I needed to know.
column13: 他们脸上的表情告诉了我我需要知道的一切。
column14: The evidence tells us that there were two robbers.
column15: 证据告诉我们有两个劫匪。
column16: The signs will tell you what exit to take off the highway.
column17: 这些标志会告诉你在高速公路上该从哪个出口驶出。

column9: + obj, not used in progressive tenses
column10: to see or understand the differences between two people or things
column11: 看出或理解两个人或事物之间的差异
column12: I can definitely tell a/the difference between the two sauces.
column13: 我绝对能分辨出这两种酱料的区别。
column14: They look exactly the same. How can you tell which is which?
column15: 它们看起来一模一样。你怎么能分辨出哪个是哪个？
column16: I can't tell who is who with their uniforms on.
column17: 他们穿上制服后，我分不清谁是谁。
column18: He is old enough to tell right from wrong. [=to know what things are good and what things are bad]
column19: 他已经足够大，能够分辨是非。

column10:
[usually used after can or could]
to see or know (something) with certainty
column11: 确定地看到或知道（某事）
column12: It was easy to tell that the bill was counterfeit.
column13: 很容易看出这张钞票是伪造的。
column14: It's hard to tell if she's kidding or not.
column15: 很难分辨她是不是在开玩笑。
column16: “He's lying.” “Really? How can you tell?”
column17: “他在说谎。” “真的吗？你怎么知道？”
column18:
I could tell (by/from the look on his face) that he was lying.
You can tell a lot about a person by the kind of car they drive.
No one can tell for sure whether it will happen.
Who can tell [=who can predict] what will happen next season?
You can never tell what type of mood he will be in.
You never can tell how he'll be feeling.
You might win the raffle—you never can tell.
As far/near as I can tell, he is happy at his new job. [=he seems to me to be happy in his new job]
column19:
我能从他脸上的表情看出来他在说谎。
你可以通过一个人开的车了解很多关于他的信息。
没有人能确定这是否会发生。
谁能预测下个赛季会发生什么？
你永远无法预料他的心情会是怎样的。
你永远无法知道他会有什么样的心情。
你也许会赢得抽奖——谁知道呢。
据我所知，他在新工作中很开心。

column10:
[This sense of one can be used in the plural form ones.]
that person or thing
column11: 那个人或事物

column13: “请给我一杯冰茶。” “我也要一杯。”
column14: Their dog died, but they plan to get another one.
column15: 他们的狗去世了，但他们打算再养一只。
column16: “You should wear the blue one.” “The one with the stripes?” “No, the other one.”
column17: “你应该穿那件蓝色的。” “有条纹的那件吗？” “不是，是另一件。”
column18:
I'd like to see the ring next to that one.
Which one did you like better?
He is the one who called the police.
Have you heard the one about [=the joke about] the priest and the rabbi?
That's one possible answer—but not the only one.
He had one too many at the bar last night. [=he had too many alcoholic drinks at the bar]
The ones on the team who are most successful practice every day.
Those batteries are the ones that still work.
column19:
我想看看那只戒指旁边的那一枚。
你更喜欢哪一个？
他就是那个报警的人。
你听过那个关于牧师和拉比的笑话吗？
那是一个可能的答案——但不是唯一的答案。
他昨晚在酒吧喝多了。
队里最成功的那些人每天都练习。
那些电池是还可以用的。

column10:
[+ of]
someone or something that is a part of a particular group
column11: 属于某个特定群体的某人或某事
column12: I met one of your friends at the party.
