column11: 以一种使某人或某物行动能力减弱的方式
column12: Remember to tie down the load.
column13: 记得把货物绑牢。
column14: They had to strap the patient down to his bed.
column15: 他们不得不用带子把病人绑在床上。

column10: in a thorough or complete way
column11: 以彻底或完整的方式
column12: The car needs to be washed down.
column13: 这辆车需要清洗一下。
column14: Hose the dog down outside.
column15: 在外面用水管给狗冲洗。

column10: to the place where a person or thing is or came from
column11: 到某人或某物所在或来自的地方
column12: They use dogs to hunt down escaped prisoners.
column13: 他们用狗来追捕逃跑的囚犯。
column14: He chased the ball down and threw it to third base.
column15: 他追着球跑过去，然后把球投向三垒。
column16: Every attempt to pin down the cause of the disease has proved unsuccessful.
column17: 每一次试图查明这种疾病的原因都未能成功。
column18: I haven't been able to track down that quotation.
column19: 我还没能找到那句话的出处。

column10: from a past time
column11: 来自过去的时间
column12: This vase has been handed down in our family for several generations.
column13: 这个花瓶在我们家已经传了好几代了。
column14: Most of these stories were passed down by word of mouth.
column15: 这些故事大多是通过口口相传流传下来的。

column10: as a first payment as a down payment
column11: 作为首付款作为定金
column12: We put 10 percent down [=we made a 10 percent down payment] on the house.
column13: 我们为这套房子支付了10%的首付。
column14: Buy a car now with no money down. [=without making a down payment]
column15: 现在购车，无需首付。

column10: in the stomach
column11: 在胃里
column12: The baby is having trouble keeping food down.
column13: 婴儿吃东西时有呕吐的情况。

column10: away from a school or university
column11: 远离学校或大学
column12: He was sent down for misconduct and never earned his degree.
column13: 他因行为不端被开除，最终未能获得学位。

column10: from a higher to a lower part of (something)
column11: 从（某物）的较高部分到较低部分
column12: She fell down the stairs.
column13: 她从楼梯上摔了下来。
column14: The children ran down the hill.
column15: 孩子们跑下了山坡。
column16: Her hair hung loosely down her back.
column17: 她的头发松散地垂在背后。
column18:
Sweat dripped down her neck.
He climbed down the ladder.
He spilled mustard down the front of his shirt.
column19:
汗水顺着她的脖子流下来。
他顺着梯子爬下来。
他把芥末洒在了衬衫前面。

column10: along the course or path of (something)
column11: 沿着（某物）的路线或路径
column12: The bathroom is halfway down the hall on the right.
column13: 浴室在走廊中间靠右边。
column14: Go down the road/street and turn left.
column15: 沿着这条路/街道走，然后向左转。
column16: There's a bridge three miles down the river. [=three miles in the same direction that the water is going in the river]
column17: 在河流下游三英里处有一座桥。
column18:
He is still pacing up and down [=back and forth in] the room.
His pitches were right down the middle of the plate.
I usually part my hair down the center.
We grew up down the block from each other.
ships sailing down the coast [=along the coast usually toward the south]
column19:
他还在房间里来回踱步。
他的投球正好在本垒板中央。
我通常把头发从中间分开。
我们小时候住在同一条街上，相隔不远。
船只沿着海岸向南航行。

column10: used to indicate that something is possible or probable
column11: 用于表示某事是可能的或很可能的
column12: They may still succeed.
column13: 他们可能仍然会成功。
column14: Do you think they may [=can, could, might] still succeed?
column15: 你认为他们还有可能成功吗？
column16: “Have they failed?” “They may have.” = (Brit) “They may have done.” [=it's possible that they failed]
column17: “他们失败了吗？” “他们可能失败了。”
column18:
You may [=might, could] be right.
If you work hard now, you may end up sitting in the boss's chair some day!
What you see may (well/very well) surprise you.
There may be some difficulties ahead.
I think he may be trying to cheat us.
It may possibly be true, mightn't it? [=(less formally) it could possibly be true, couldn't it?]
May it not [=mightn't it, (less formally) couldn't it] after all turn out to be true?
This vacation may [=might] not be so bad after all.
When you're older, you may understand.
We may go if they ask us, but then again we may not.
As you may or may not have heard, we've won!
column19:
你也许是对的。
如果你现在努力工作，将来有一天你可能会坐上老板的位子！
你看到的东西很可能会让你感到惊讶。
前方可能会有一些困难。
我觉得他可能在试图欺骗我们。
这也许是真的，不是吗？
它最终难道不会是真的吗？
这次假期说不定其实没那么糟。
等你长大了，可能就会明白了。
如果他们邀请我们，我们也许会去，但也可能不会去。
你可能已经听说了，也可能还没听说，我们赢了！

column10: used to say that one thing is true but something else is also true
column11: 用来说一件事情是对的，但另一件事情也同样成立。
column12: He may [=might] be slow, but he does very good work. = Slow though he may be, he (still) does very good work. [=although he's slow, he does very good work]
column13: 他可能动作慢，但他工作做得非常好。
column14: It may [=might] be cold outside, but it's still a beautiful day. [=although it's cold outside, it's still a beautiful day]
column15: 外面可能很冷，但今天依然是美好的一天。
column16: She may [=might] have been a great actress, but she was a terrible parent.
column17: 她也许曾是一位出色的女演员，但却是一个糟糕的家长。

column10:
[compare can]
used to indicate that something is allowed
column11: 用于表示某事是被允许的。
column12: You may go now. [=you have permission to leave now]
column13: 你现在可以走了。
column14: No one may enter without a ticket.
column15: 没有票不得入内。
column16: The children may play wherever they choose.
column17: 孩子们可以在他们选择的任何地方玩耍。
column18: You may tell me your opinion, but I won't change my mind.
column19: 你可以告诉我你的看法，但我不会改变主意。

column10:
[compare can]
used to ask a question or make a request in a polite way
column11: 用于以礼貌的方式提问或提出请求
column12: “May [=might] I borrow your pen?” “Of course you may!”
column13: “我可以借用你的笔吗？” “当然可以！”
column14: “May I help you,” asked the waiter, “or are you already being served?”
column15: “请问需要我帮忙吗？”服务员问道，“还是已经有人为您服务了？”
column16: May I ask who is calling?
column17: 请问您是哪位？
column18: “May I leave a little early today?” “No, you may not.”
column19: “我今天可以早点离开吗？” “不，你不可以。”

column10: used to express a wish
column11: 用来表达愿望
column12: Long may the Queen reign! [=I hope the Queen will reign for a long time]
column13: 女王万岁！
column14: May the best man win!
column15: 愿最优秀的人获胜！
column16: May you have a long and happy life!
column17: 愿你拥有长久而幸福的生活！

column10: used to make a polite suggestion
column11: 用于提出礼貌的建议
column12: You may [=might] want to think again and consider your options carefully.
column13: 你也许想要再三考虑，并仔细权衡你的选择。
column14: It may [=might] be wise to proceed cautiously.
column15: 谨慎行事可能是明智的。

column10: used in various polite expressions with I
column11: 与“I”一起用于各种礼貌表达中
column12: May I just say how pleased I am to be here. [=I would like to say how pleased I am to be here]
column13: 我想说我非常高兴能在这里。
column14: If I may (interrupt you), would you please repeat the answer?
column15: 如果可以的话（打断一下），请您重复一下答案好吗？
column16: I'd like to ask a question, if I may.
column17: 如果可以的话，我想问一个问题。
column18: This has been, if I may say so, one of the happiest days of my life.
column19: 如果可以这样说的话，这是我人生中最幸福的日子之一。

column10: used to indicate the reason for something or the purpose of something
column11: 用于表示某事的原因或某事的目的
column12: We exercise so that we may [=will] be strong and healthy. [=we exercise in order to be strong and healthy]
column13: 我们锻炼是为了变得强壮和健康。
column14: I work hard so that my family may [=will] not go hungry.
column15: 我努力工作，这样我的家人就不会挨饿。

column10: the fifth month of the year
column11: 一年中的第五个月
column12: in (early/middle/mid-/late) May
column13: 在五月（上旬/中旬/中-/下旬）
column14: early/late in May
column15: 五月初/五月底
column16: We arrived on May the fourth. = (US) We arrived on May fourth. = We arrived on the fourth of May.
column17: 我们是在五月四日到达的。
column18:
April showers bring May flowers. [=rain in April causes flowers to bloom in May]
Shakespeare called it “the merry month of May.”
The last two Mays have been cold and rainy.
column19:
四月的阵雨带来五月的花朵。
莎士比亚称其为“欢乐的五月”。
过去的两个五月都又冷又多雨。

column10: at a time following (something or someone) later than (something or someone)
column11: 在（某事或某人）之后的某个时间，晚于（某事或某人）
column12: He returned after 20 years.
column13: 他在二十年后回来了。
column14: I stood up after the judge (did). [=the judge stood up before I (did)]
column15: 法官站起来后，我才站起来。
column16: He left after an hour.
column17: 他一个小时后离开了。
column18:
They earned $30,000 after (paying) taxes.
We arrived shortly after six o'clock.
She hasn't lived there since (the time) after the war.
before, during, and after the war
He left just/right/immediately/soon/shortly after nightfall/dark.
Call me after your arrival.
He finished the exam after me.
The job got easier after a while. [=after some time had passed]
Night fell, and soon after that [=soon afterward] he left.
Let's get going! It's after [=past] 12 (o'clock).
She was going to arrive tomorrow but I'm now expecting her the day after tomorrow instead.
column19:
他们在缴税后赚了30,000美元。
我们在六点过后不久到达。
自从（战后）那段时间起，她就没有再住在那里了。
战争前、期间和之后
他在天黑/夜幕降临后刚/正/立刻/很快/不久就离开了。
你到达后给我打电话。
他在我之后完成了考试。
过了一段时间后，这份工作变得容易了。
夜幕降临，不久之后他就离开了。
我们走吧！现在已经过了12点了。
她原本明天到，但我现在预计她会在后天到。

column10: used to describe a time following a specified hour
column11: 用来描述在指定时间之后的时段
column12: It's 20 (minutes) after 12. [=it's 20 past 12; it's 12:20]
column13: 现在是12点过20分。

column10: following and because of (something)
column11: 跟随并因为（某事）
column12: After all our advice, she's certain to do better. [=she's certain to do better because we have given her our advice]
column13: 在我们给了她所有建议之后，她肯定会做得更好。

column10: following and in spite of (something)
column11: 在……之后，尽管（某事）
column12: How can you say that after what happened last night?
column13: 在昨晚发生了那样的事情之后，你怎么还能这么说？
column14: Even after all our advice, she still did badly! [=she did badly even though we gave her our advice]
column15: 即使在我们给了她所有建议之后，她还是表现得很糟糕！

column10: following (something or someone) in order or in a series
column11: 跟随（某事或某人）以便顺序或按系列进行
column12: The number 2 comes before 3 and after 1. [=2 comes between 1 and 3]
column13: 数字2在3之前，在1之后。
column14: It's the highest mountain after Mount Everest.
column15: 它是仅次于珠穆朗玛峰的最高山峰。
column16: You'll see my house just before the bank and after the school.
column17: 你会在银行前面、学校后面看到我的房子。
column18:
[The phrase after you is used as a polite way of saying that someone should go ahead of you or do something before you do it.] After you, Madam!
[In British English, you can say after you with something to ask the person who is using something to let you use it next.] After you with the pencil, please. [=I would like to use the pencil when you have finished using it]
The children marched out one after the other in single file.
You go first and I'll go/follow after you.
My name is listed after yours.
column19:
您请先，女士！
用完铅笔后请给我。
孩子们一个接一个地排成单行走了出去。
你先走，我随后就来/跟着你走。
我的名字排在你的后面。

column10: used in phrases to describe something that happens many times or for a long period of time
column11: 用于短语中，描述某事发生多次或持续很长一段时间。
column12: He's done the same thing time after time.
column13: 他一次又一次地做了同样的事情。
column14: They have suffered misfortune after misfortune. [=they have suffered a long series of misfortunes]
column15: 他们接连遭遇了一次又一次的不幸。
column16: She does her job day after day without complaining.
column17: 她日复一日地做着自己的工作，从不抱怨。
column18: Wave after [=upon] wave was beating against the shore.
column19: 一波接一波地拍打着海岸。

column10: trying to catch or get (something or someone)
column11: 试图抓住或获得（某物或某人）
column12: [If people are after you to do something, they want you to do it and they tell you to do it repeatedly.] Mom was after me to clean my room. [=Mom repeatedly told me to clean my room]
column13: 妈妈一直催我打扫房间。
column14: The police are after him. [=are trying to catch him]
column15: 警察正在追捕他。
column16: The dog ran after the ball. [=the dog ran to get the ball]
column17: 狗追着球跑。
column18:
The police went/chased after the escaped criminal.
What do you think he's after with all his questions? [=what is he trying to achieve by asking his questions?]
column19:
警察追捕逃犯。
你觉得他问这么多问题是想达到什么目的？

column10: following the actions or departure of (someone)
column11: 跟随（某人）的行动或离开
column12: She called/shouted after him as he walked away. [=she called/shouted at/toward him as he walked away]
column13: 当他走开时，她在他身后喊叫/大声叫喊。
column14: If you make a mess, don't expect me to clean up after you.
column15: 如果你弄乱了什么，别指望我帮你收拾。
column16: They made a mess and didn't clean up after themselves. [=they didn't clean up the mess they made]
column17: 他们弄得一团糟，却没有自己收拾。

column10: with the name of (someone or something)
column11: 以（某人或某物）的名字
column12: The game rugby was named after Rugby School in England, where it began.
column13: 橄榄球这项运动的名称来源于英国的拉格比学校，正是在那里它诞生的。
column14: He was called George after his father.
column15: 他以父亲的名字被取名为乔治。
column16: She was named after her grandmother. [=she was given the same name as her grandmother]
column17: 她是以她祖母的名字命名的。

column10: in the manner of (someone or something)
column11: 以（某人或某事）的方式
column12: (formal) a story after (the manner of) Hemingway
column13: （正式）一则仿照海明威风格的故事
column14: a building patterned after [=on] a cathedral
column15: 一座仿照大教堂设计的建筑

column10: in a lower or less important position than (something)
column11: 处于比（某物）更低或不太重要的位置
column12: They put quality after quantity. [=they cared more about quantity than about quality]
column13: 他们把数量放在质量之前。

column10: about or concerning (someone or something)
column11: 关于（某人或某事）
column12: I met one of your old friends and she was asking/inquiring after you. [=she was asking about you; she was asking how you are]
column13: 我遇到了你的一位老朋友，她在打听你的情况。
column14: She was asking after your health.
column15: 她在询问你的健康状况。

column10: used to say or suggest that something is the proper, reasonable, or best thing to do
column11: 用来说或暗示某事是恰当的、合理的或最好的做法
column12: You should [=ought to] get some rest.
column13: 你应该休息一下。
column14: They should be punished.
column15: 他们应该受到惩罚。
column16: We should leave a few minutes early to make sure we get there on time.
column17: 我们应该提前几分钟出发，以确保准时到达。
column18:
Maybe you should consider finding a new job.
I should emphasize that these numbers are only estimates.
My friends say that I should quit the team.
What time should we meet? [=what is the best time for us to meet?; what time do you want to meet?]
Patients should inform the receptionist upon their arrival.
column19:
也许你应该考虑找一份新工作。
我应该强调，这些数字只是估算值。
我的朋友们说我应该退出团队。
我们应该几点见面？
病人到达时应告知接待员。

column10: used with have to say that something was the proper, reasonable, or best thing to do but was not done
column11: 用于与 have 连用，表示某事本来是合适的、合理的或最好的做法，但实际上并没有做。
column12: You should have been more careful.
column13: 你本应该更小心一点。
column14: She shouldn't have spoken to him so rudely.
column15: 她本不应该那样无礼地跟他说话。
column16: What should I have done?
column17: 我本应该怎么做？
column18:
Should I not have gone? [=was it wrong for me to go?]
I should have known that he would be late. [=I didn't know that he would be late, but it would have been reasonable for me to expect it because he is often late]
column19:
我本不该去吗？
我早该知道他会迟到。

column10: used with have to say that you wish someone had seen, heard, or experienced something
column11: 用在 have 后，表示你希望某人曾经看到、听到或经历过某事。
column12: You should have seen her face [=I wish that you had seen her face] when she opened the present.
column13: 你应该看看她打开礼物时的表情。
column14: It was so funny. You should have been there.
column15: 太有趣了。你本应该在场的。

column10: used to ask for someone's opinion
column11: 用来询问某人的意见
column12: When shall we leave? [=when do you think we should leave?]
column13: 我们什么时候离开？
column14: “Shall [=should] I call a taxi?” “Please do.”
column15: “我需要叫辆出租车吗？” “请叫吧。”
column16: Let's dance, shall we?
column17: 我们跳舞吧，好吗？
column18:
Shall we dance? [=would you like to dance?]
Should [=(more formally) shall] I turn the music down?
What should we have for lunch?
column19:
我们跳舞好吗？
我应该把音乐调小声一点吗？
我们午饭吃什么好呢？

column10: used to say that something is expected or correct
column11: 用来说某事是预期的或正确的
column12: Everyone should [=ought to] have a copy of the handout.
column13: 每个人都应该有一份讲义。
column14: There should be four place settings at the table, not six.
column15: 桌子上应该有四套餐具，而不是六套。
column16: “He feels very sorry about what happened.” “Well, he should!”
column17: “他对发生的事情感到非常抱歉。” “嗯，他就应该这样！”
column18:
You should be ashamed of yourself, behaving so rudely to our guests!
They should be here by now. = They should have arrived by now. [=I expected them to be here by now]
column19:
你应该为自己感到羞愧，对我们的客人如此无礼！
他们现在应该已经到了。

column10: used when saying that you feel a specified way about someone's words or behavior
column11: 用于表达你对某人言语或行为有某种特定感受时
column12: I'm surprised that he should intentionally be so rude to you.
column13: 我很惊讶他竟然会故意对你这么无礼。
column14: It's strange (that) you should say that.
column15: 你这么说真奇怪。
column16: Funny you should mention it. [=I think it's odd/strange that you mentioned it] I've been thinking the same thing.
column17: 你提到这件事真有意思。 我也一直在想同样的事情。

column10: used to emphasize what you believe, think, hope, etc.
column11: 用于强调你所相信、认为、希望等的内容。
column12: I should imagine it won't take more than two hours to drive there. [=I am fairly certain that it won't take more than two hours]
column13: 我想开车到那里应该不会超过两个小时。
column14: I should think not. [=I really don't think so]
column15: 我认为不是。
column16: I should hope that she would apologize. [=I expect her to apologize]
column17: 我希望她会道歉。
column18: “She apologized for her rude behavior.” “Well, I should hope so!”
column19: “她为自己的无礼行为道歉了。” “嗯，那是应该的！”

column10: used with have in negative statements as a polite way of thanking someone for doing something
column11: 与 have 连用在否定句中，用作对某人做某事表示礼貌的感谢方式。
column12: You really should not have gone to all that trouble on my account—but I'm glad you did!
column13: 你真的不必为了我费这么大劲——但我很高兴你这么做了！
column14: Flowers for me? You shouldn't have.
column15: 给我送花？你太客气了。

column10:
[usually used with if]
used to talk about the result or effect of something that may happen or be true
column11: 用于谈论某件可能发生或为真的事情的结果或影响

column18: The company is working hard to stay/keep ahead of the field. [=to continue to be more successful than its competitors]

column10: a region or space in which an effect or force (such as gravity, electricity, or magnetism) exists

column12: an electric/magnetic field

column10: an area in which a particular type of information is placed

column13: 您必须在提交表单前填写所有字段。
column14: (computers) The database is separated into several different fields.
column15: （计算机）数据库被分为几个不同的字段。

column13: 在他的视野中没有任何东西移动。

column15: 我们还能在哪里见面？

column18:

column19:
我们决定去别的地方吃晚饭。
我不知道我们还能什么时候去。

column10: used to refer to a different or additional person or thing
column11: 用来指代不同的或额外的人或事物

column13: 他把友谊看得比任何东西都重要。

column15: 那是别人的问题。
column16: If all else fails, surgery is an option.
column17: 如果所有其他方法都失败了，手术是一个选择。

What else did he say?

Who else is coming to the party?

There isn't much else [=more] going on.

column19:
除了他之外，还得有其他人来做这件事。
他还说了什么？
没有别的事情可做了。
还有谁要来参加聚会？
你还想要别的什么吗？
没有太多其他的事情发生。
如果说没有别的优点，食物至少很便宜。

column10:
[often + by] [often + by]
to move past someone or something
column11: 经过某人或某物
column12: The boat was too tall to pass beneath/under the bridge.
column13: 这艘船太高，无法从桥下通过。
column14: A flock of geese were passing overhead.
column15: 一群大雁从头顶飞过。
column16: Stand here and don't let anyone pass. [=move past you]
column17: 站在这里，不要让任何人通过。
column18:
They pass by the library on their way to school.
I was just passing by and thought I'd stop and say hello.
They pass the library every morning on their way to school.
The ships passed each other in the night.
We passed each other in the hallway without looking up.
She was hoping he would stop and talk to her, but he passed her by.
column19:
他们在去学校的路上经过图书馆。
我只是路过，想着停下来打个招呼。
他们每天早上去学校的路上都会经过图书馆。
这些船在夜里相互驶过。
我们在走廊里擦肩而过，彼此都没有抬头。
她希望他能停下来和她说话，但他却径直走了过去。

column10: to move past someone or something that is moving more slowly in the same direction
column11: 超过某人或某物（指在同一方向上移动得更慢的人或物）
column12: (US) “Is it safe to pass?” [=(Brit) overtake] “No, there's a car coming in the other lane.”
column13: （美）“现在超车安全吗？” “不安全，对面车道有辆车过来了。”
column14: She passed two other runners just before the finish line.
column15: 她在接近终点线时超过了另外两名跑步者。
column16: He passed the slower cars on the highway.
column17: 他在高速公路上超越了较慢的汽车。

column10:
[often + through]
to move or go into or through a particular place
column11: 进入或穿过某个特定地方
column12: The drug passes quickly into the bloodstream.
column13: 该药物很快进入血液循环。
column14: In a solar eclipse, the moon passes between the sun and the Earth.
column15: 在日食中，月亮经过太阳和地球之间。
column16: The airplane passed out of sight.
column17: 飞机消失在视线之外。
column18:
Fear and panic passed through the crowd.
A river passes through the middle of the city.
Millions of tourists pass through the museum every year.
The paper passes through the fax machine and comes out the other end.
The bullet passed through his shoulder.
We passed through Texas on our way to Mexico.
We're just passing through. [=staying here for a very short time]
column19:
恐惧和恐慌在人群中蔓延。
一条河流穿过城市的中心。
每年有数百万游客参观这个博物馆。
纸张通过传真机，从另一端出来。
子弹穿过了他的肩膀。
我们在去墨西哥的路上经过了德克萨斯州。
我们只是路过这里。

column10: to cause (something) to move or go in a specified way
column11: 使（某物）以特定方式移动或前进

column13: 将绳子的末端穿过环。
column14: He passed the rope around the pole.
column15: 他把绳子绕在杆子上。

column10: to give (something) to someone using your hands
column11: 用你的手把（某物）递给某人

column13: 她把婴儿还给了他的母亲。
column14: Would you please pass the salt?
column15: 请把盐递给我好吗？
column16: Pass [=hand] me the butter, please.
column17: 请把黄油递给我。
column18:
They started passing around pictures of their trip.
Take one sheet and pass the rest down/on/along. [=take one sheet and give the rest to the next person]
Can you pass that screwdriver over to me?
column19:
他们开始传看他们旅行的照片。
拿一张纸，把剩下的传下去。
你能把那把螺丝刀递给我吗？

column10: to throw, hit, or kick a ball or puck to a teammate
column11: 把球或冰球扔、击打或踢给队友
column12: Pass me the ball! = Pass the ball to me!
column13: 把球传给我！
column14: She passed to her teammate who then scored a goal.
column15: 她把球传给了队友，队友随后进球得分。

column10:
[often + on] [sometimes + along]
to cause someone to have or be affected by (something that you have had or been affected by)
column11: 使某人拥有或受到（你曾经拥有或受到的某事）的影响
column12: The disease was passed from mother to child. = She passed the disease to her child.
column13: 这种疾病是从母亲传给孩子的。
column14: She contracted the disease and passed it on to her child.
column15: 她感染了这种疾病，并把它传染给了她的孩子。
column16: Gas prices have risen, forcing companies to pass the cost on to the consumer.
column17: 油价上涨，迫使公司将成本转嫁给消费者。
column18:
We lowered our costs and are now able to pass on the savings to our customers.
We're passing the savings along to our customers.
column19:
我们降低了成本，现在能够将节省下来的费用回馈给我们的客户。
我们正在将节省下来的费用让利给客户。

column10:
[often + on] [often + along]
to give (information) to another person
column11: 向他人传递（信息）

column13: 医生需要将这些信息传达给他们的病人。
column14: Everyone's invited to the party. Pass it on! [=tell people that everyone is invited]
column15: 每个人都被邀请参加聚会。传达下去！

column17: 他们很快就把会议推迟的消息传达了出去。
column18: He told me about it, and now I'm passing it along to you.
column19: 他告诉了我这件事，现在我把它转告给你。

column10: to go from one person to another person
column11: 从一个人到另一个人

column13: 这个谣言很快在人们之间传开了。
column14: The book passed from hand to hand.
column15: 这本书被人们传来传去。

column10: to be given to someone especially according to a law, rule, etc.
column11: 给予某人，尤其是根据法律、规则等。

column13: 王位传给了国王的儿子。
column14: Ownership passes to the buyer upon payment in full.
column15: 所有权在全额付款后转移给买方。
column16: After her death, the house passed into the hands of her granddaughter. [=her granddaughter became the owner of the house]
column17: 她去世后，这所房子归她的孙女所有。

column10: to go by
column11: （时间）过去，流逝；经过（某处）

column13: 几个月过去了，我才收到回复。
column14: He became sleepy as the time passed.
column15: 随着时间的流逝，他变得昏昏欲睡。
column16: The days pass quickly when you're on vacation.
column17: 当你在度假时，日子过得很快。
column18: Another day passed without any news about the whereabouts of their missing son.
column19: 又一天过去了，关于他们失踪儿子的下落依然没有任何消息。

column10: to let (time or a period of time) go by especially while you are doing something enjoyable
column11: 让（时间或一段时间）流逝，尤其是在你做一些令人愉快的事情时。
column12: He passes [=spends] his days reading and taking walks around the neighborhood.
column13: 他每天都在阅读和在附近散步中度过。
column14: They passed the evening playing cards.
column15: 他们晚上打牌度过了时光。

column17: 我们在公交车上玩游戏打发时间。
column18: I walked over to my neighbor's house to pass the time of day. [=to have a friendly and informal conversation]
column19: 我走到邻居家去闲聊打发时间。

column10:

column11: 发生或进行

The era of the traveling salesman has passed into history. [=traveling salesmen no longer exist]
column19:
他们一直等到危险已经过去才行动。
他们曾经很幸福，但那段时光已经过去了。
推销员的时代已经成为历史。

column10: to be done, said, etc., without producing a response

column15: 她对他的话没有作出评论。

column10:
[often + on]
to not take, accept, or use something that is offered to you

column10:

to die

column17: 两个曾经的朋友

[opposite buy]
to exchange (something) for money
column11:
[反义词 buy]
出售（某物）换取金钱

column13: 他把他的车卖了。

to be able to be bought for a particular price

column18:
The dictionary is selling well. [=many people are buying copies of the dictionary]

column19:
这本词典卖得很好。
最新款就是卖不出去。

column10: used to say how many copies of something have been sold

column11: 非常重要

column13: 一位重要的诗人/艺术家

column14: They broke the corporation (up) into several smaller companies.

column16: The corporation broke (up) into several smaller companies.
column17: 该公司被拆分成了几家较小的公司。

column10: to go through or make a hole in (a surface, someone's skin, etc.)
column11: 穿过或在（表面、某人的皮肤等）上打一个洞

column14: A large fish broke the surface of the water.
column15: 一条大鱼冲破水面。

column10:
[usually used figuratively]
to go through (something) by using force
column11: 用武力穿过（某物）

column13: 用刀子打开封条。
column14: The ceremony is to celebrate people who broke racial barriers in the music industry.
column15: 该仪式旨在表彰那些打破音乐行业种族壁垒的人。

column10: to cut into and turn over the surface of (the ground, soil, etc.)
column11: 切入并翻转（地面、土壤等）的表层
column12: The farmer uses a plow to break the soil.
column13: 农民用犁来翻土。

column10: to fail to do what is required by (a law, a promise, etc.)
column11: 未能履行（法律、承诺等）所要求的事项
column12: She may not have broken the law, but she acted wrongly.
column13: 她也许没有违法，但她的行为是错误的。
column14: You broke your promise.
column15: 你违背了你的承诺。
column16: Students who break the rules will be punished.
column17: 违反规定的学生将会受到惩罚。
column18:
He broke the contract by failing to make the payments on time.
You can get fined for breaking the speed limit. [=for driving faster than you are legally allowed to drive]
column19:
他因未能按时付款而违反了合同。
超速驾驶会被罚款。

column10: to destroy or defeat (something) by using force or pressure
column11: 通过使用武力或压力来摧毁或击败（某物）
column12: They kept putting pressure on him, but they couldn't break his spirit/determination/resistance.
column13: 他们一直在给他施加压力，但他们无法摧毁他的意志/决心/抵抗。
column14: They finally broke his will to resist.
column15: 他们终于摧毁了他反抗的意志。
column16: His spirit/determination will never break.
column17: 他的精神/决心永远不会被打破。

column10: to defeat or ruin (someone) to cause (someone) to fail or to stop trying or fighting
column11: 击败或毁掉（某人）；使（某人）失败，或让（某人）停止尝试或斗争
column12: He swore that he would break his rivals/competitors.
column13: 他发誓要击垮他的对手/竞争者。
column14: They kept putting pressure on him, but they couldn't break him.
column15: 他们一直在给他施加压力，但他们无法击垮他。
column16: These huge losses are going to break [=ruin] me financially!
column17: 这些巨大的损失会让我在经济上破产！
column18: This film could make or break her career. [=the success or failure of her career could depend on the success or failure of this film]
column19: 这部电影可能会成就或毁掉她的事业。

column10:
[usually + under]
to lose your health, mental or physical strength, or control
column11: 失去健康、精神或体力，或失去控制
column12: The witness broke under questioning.
column13: 证人在讯问下崩溃了。
column14: I was afraid I would break under the strain of constant uncertainty.
column15: 我害怕自己会在持续的不确定压力下崩溃。

column10: to train (a wild animal) to behave in a way that is useful to people
column11: 训练（野生动物）以对人类有用的方式行事
column12: special equipment used to break horses
column13: 用于驯服马匹的专用设备

column10: to cause the end of (something that is strong or that has continued for a long time)
column11: 导致（某种强大或持续很久的事物）的终结
column12: A group of moderates from both parties are negotiating to break the deadlock in Congress.
column13: 来自两党的温和派正在进行谈判，以打破国会的僵局。
column14: Many people in the industry were very upset when the government broke the strike.
column15: 当政府镇压罢工时，业界的许多人都感到非常不满。
column16: He decided to break all ties/links with them. [=to end all connections with them]
column17: 他决定与他们断绝一切关系。
column18:
She scored a goal in the last minute of the game, breaking a 2-2 tie.
It's never easy to break [=kick, give up] a bad habit.
column19:
她在比赛的最后一分钟进球，打破了2比2的平局。
改掉坏习惯从来都不容易。

column10:
[+ of]
to cause (someone) to give up a habit
column11: 使（某人）戒除习惯
column12: His friends have tried everything to break him of his smoking habit. [=have tried everything to make him stop smoking]
column13: 他的朋友们已经尝试了一切方法来让他戒烟。

column10: to interrupt (something)
column11: 打断（某事）
column12: The peaceful silence of the evening was broken by a sudden shout.
column13: 傍晚的宁静被一声突如其来的喊叫打破了。
column14: The commotion broke my train of thought.
column15: 骚动打断了我的思路。
column16: The sudden noise broke my concentration. [=made it impossible for me to concentrate]
column17: 突然的噪音打断了我的注意力。
column18:
Sometimes I sing while I'm driving, just to break (up) the monotony of my commute.
The horizon line was broken only by a few stands of trees in the distance.
The planes broke formation [=stopped flying together in an organized group] and took off in different directions.
column19:
有时候我开车时会唱歌，只是为了打破通勤的单调。
远处只有几片树林打破了地平线的连贯。
飞机们打破了队形（即不再有组织地一起飞行），朝不同方向飞去。

column10: to cause (something, such as a curse or spell) to no longer be effective
column11: 使（某物，如诅咒或咒语）不再生效
column12: a mystic who claimed to be able to break curses
column13: 一位自称能够破除诅咒的神秘主义者

column10: to stop an activity (such as working) for a brief period of time
column11: 暂停一项活动（例如工作）一小段时间
column12: Let's break for lunch. [=let's take a break for lunch; let's temporarily stop working and eat lunch]
column13: 我们休息一下去吃午饭吧。

column10: to tell (bad news) to someone in a kind or gentle way
column11: 以一种善意或温和的方式把（坏消息）告诉某人
column12: I know she'll be very upset when she finds out she didn't get the job, so please try to break it to her gently.
column13: 我知道当她发现自己没有得到这份工作时会非常难过，所以请尽量温和地把这个消息告诉她。

column10: to make (something, such as news) publicly known for the first time
column11: 首次公开（某事，例如新闻）
column12: The local TV station was the first to break the news about the President's visit.
column13: 当地电视台是第一个报道总统来访消息的。

column10: to become publicly known
column11: 为公众所知
column12: The story broke yesterday. [=the story was reported for the first time yesterday]
column13: 这个消息是昨天首次报道的。
column14: People were shocked when (news of) the scandal first broke.
column15: 丑闻消息刚刚曝光时，人们感到震惊。

column10: to reduce the speed or force of (something)
column11: 减少（某物）的速度或力度
column12: The bushes beneath the window helped to break his fall. [=helped make his fall less forceful]
column13: 窗户下的灌木丛帮助缓冲了他的坠落。
column14: She walked straight across the room without breaking (her) stride. [=without pausing or slowing down]
column15: 她径直穿过房间，步伐没有丝毫停顿。

column10: to be higher or more than (a specified number, measurement, etc.)
column11: 高于或多于（指定的数字、测量值等）
column12: The temperature is expected to break 90 (degrees Fahrenheit) today.
column13: 预计今天气温将突破90华氏度。

column10: to do better than (a record)
column11: 打破（纪录）
column12: She ran a great race and almost broke the world record. [=she almost ran the race faster than anyone in the world has ever run it]
column13: 她跑得非常出色，几乎打破了世界纪录。
column14: He set a record that may never be broken.
column15: 他创造了一项可能永远无法被打破的纪录。

column10: to have a score that is lower than or higher than (a specified total)
column11: 分数低于或高于（指定总分）
column12: golfers trying to break 90 [=to have a score below 90]
column13: 试图打破90杆的高尔夫球手
column14: bowlers trying to break 200 [=to have a score above 200]
column15: 试图突破200分的保龄球手

column10: to find or provide an explanation or solution for (something, such as a criminal case)
column11: 为（某事，例如刑事案件）寻找或提供解释或解决方案
column12: The detective finally broke [=solved] the case.
column13: 侦探终于破了这个案子。
column14: The detective found the evidence that broke the case.
column15: 侦探找到了破案的证据。

column10: to find the meaning of (a secret code)
column11: 找出（秘密代码）的含义
column12: A team of experts was finally able to break the code and decipher the meaning of the message.
column13: 一组专家最终成功破解了密码，并解读了信息的含义。

column10: to change by becoming rainy, clear, cool, etc., after a long time
column11: 在很长一段时间后，天气变得多雨、晴朗、凉爽等。
column12: waiting for the weather to break
column13: 等待天气好转
column14: The heat wave should finally break [=end] tomorrow.
column15: 热浪预计明天终于会结束。

column10: to separate so that the sky or sun can be seen
column11: 分开，以便可以看到天空或太阳
column12: The clouds broke and the fog dissipated, revealing blue sky above.
column13: 乌云散开，雾气消散，露出了上方的蓝天。

column10: to start suddenly
column11: 突然开始
column12: Everyone ran to get indoors when the storm broke. [=when it began to rain]
column13: 暴风雨来临时，大家都跑到室内去了。

column10: to begin when the sun rises
column11: 在太阳升起时开始
column12: They left just as day was breaking. [=just as the sun was rising]
column13: 他们离开时正值天刚破晓。
column14: The dawn was breaking.
column15: 黎明破晓了。

column10: to begin running quickly
column11: 开始快速奔跑
column12: Everyone broke [=dashed, ran] for cover.
column13: 每个人都冲向掩护。

column10: to stop fighting and run away
column11: 停止战斗并逃跑
column12: When the enemy charged, our troops broke and ran.
column13: 当敌人发起冲锋时，我军溃败逃跑了。

column10: to give smaller bills or coins for (a large bill)
column11: 为（大额纸币）兑换成较小面额的纸币或硬币
column12: Can you break [=change] a $20 bill for me?
column13: 你能帮我把一张20美元的钞票换开吗？

column10: to use (a large bill) to pay for something that costs much less than the value of the bill
column11: 用一张大额钞票支付远低于该钞票面值的物品

column13: 我不想为了买一美元的东西而破开一张二十美元的钞票。

column10: to curl over and fall onto or near land
column11: 卷曲并落在陆地上或靠近陆地
column12: the sound of waves breaking against/over/on the rocks
column13: 海浪拍打在岩石上的声音

column10: to change sharply in tone or pitch because of strong emotion
column11: 由于强烈的情感而语调或音高急剧变化
column12: Her voice was breaking with emotion as she said goodbye.
column13: 她在道别时声音因情绪激动而哽咽。

column10: to change from the high voice of a boy to the lower voice of a man
column11: 从男孩的高音变为男人的低音
column12: an adolescent boy whose voice is breaking
column13: 一个正在变声的青春期男孩

column9: no obj, of a thrown or struck ball, sports
column10: to turn or curve
column11: 转动或弯曲

column13: 当推杆球接近球洞时，它向左偏移了。

column15: 一种从击球手身边偏离的投球
column16: The pitcher threw a breaking ball. [=a pitch that curves]
column17: 投手投出了一个变速球。

column10: to win against (an opponent who is serving)
column11: 在（对方发球时）获胜

column13: 挑战者在最后一盘破掉了冠军的发球局。

column15: 挑战者在决胜盘中破发，但冠军随即回破，将比分扳平。

column10: to happen or develop
column11: 发生或发展

column13: 为了让团队取得成功，一切都必须顺利进行。
column14: Things have been breaking [=going] well for the company in the past six months.
column15: 在过去的六个月里，公司一切进展顺利。

column10: in a better way
column11: 以更好的方式

column13: “她在学校表现怎么样？” “她一开始表现不好，但现在好多了。”
column14: She sings better than I do.
column15: 她唱得比我好。
column16: He sings better than he acts.
column17: 他的歌唱得比表演得好。

“Instead of writing to her, I'm going to visit her in person.” “Even better.”
column19:
你可以给她写信，或者，更好的是，亲自去看她。
“我打算亲自去看她，而不是给她写信。” “那更好了。”

column10: used to suggest that something should or should not be done
column11: 用来建议某事应该或不应该做

column13: 有些事情最好不要说出来。
column14: You would do better to leave now [=you should leave now] if you want to get there on time.
column15: 如果你想准时到那里，你最好现在就离开。

column10: to a higher or greater degree
column11: 到更高或更大的程度

column13: 他比你更了解这个故事。

column11: 距离或数量上更大，更多

column13: 到下一个镇还有九英里多。
column14: It's better than an hour's drive to the lake.
column15: 到湖边开车要一个多小时。

column10:

the quality that makes one person or thing unlike another

column13: 她知道是非对错的区别。

column15: 这两栋房子没有区别。它们看起来一模一样。
column16: There's a striking difference in the sisters' looks. [=they look very different from each other]
column17: 这对姐妹的外貌有着显著的差异。
column18:
It's hard to tell the difference [=distinguish] between one action movie and another.
The new version is supposed to be much better than the old one, but I can't tell the difference (between them).
column19:
很难分辨一部动作片和另一部动作片之间的区别。
新版据说比旧版好得多，但我分辨不出它们之间的区别。

column10: something that people do not agree about a disagreement in opinion
column11: 人们不同意的事情，意见上的分歧

column13: 他们一直以来都有分歧。
column14: The debate gave them a chance to air their differences. [=to discuss the things that they disagree about]
column15: 这场辩论给了他们一个机会来表达他们的分歧。
column16: We need to find a way to resolve/settle our differences. [=to stop disagreeing, arguing, etc.]
column17: 我们需要找到一种方法来解决/化解我们的分歧。
column18:
There seems to be a difference of opinion [=people disagree] about what we should do next.
They divorced because of irreconcilable differences. [=serious disagreements that they were not able to settle]
column19:
关于我们接下来应该做什么，似乎存在意见分歧。
他们因为不可调和的分歧而离婚。

column10: the degree or amount by which things differ
column11: 事物之间差异的程度或数量

column13: 价格有很大差异。
column14: There's a 15-year age difference between her oldest and youngest children. [=her oldest child is fifteen years older than her youngest child]
column15: 她最大的孩子和最小的孩子之间相差15岁。

column10: to get or be given (something)
column11: 获得或被给予（某物）
column12: You will be charged a late fee if the electric company does not receive your payment on time.
column13: 如果电力公司没有按时收到您的付款，您将被收取滞纳金。
column14: I received a letter/call from her yesterday.
column15: 我昨天收到了她的一封信/一个电话。
column16: You will receive a discount if you spend over $100.
column17: 如果您的消费超过100美元，您将获得折扣。
column18: This spring he'll receive [=be awarded] his PhD in physics.
column19: 今年春天，他将获得物理学博士学位。

column10:
[often used as (be) received]
to react to (something) in a specified way
column11: 以特定方式对（某事）作出反应

column13: 她以异常平静的态度接受了他去世的消息。
column14: Her new book was well/poorly received by the critics. [=the critics liked/disliked her new book]
column15: 她的新书受到了评论家的好评/差评。
column16: The results of the study were received with considerable skepticism.
column17: 该研究结果受到了相当大的怀疑。

column10: to welcome (someone) in usually a formal way
column11: 通常以正式的方式欢迎（某人）
column12: The ambassador received [=greeted] his guests as they arrived at the party.
column13: 大使在宾客们到达聚会时接待了他们。

column10:
[+ into]
to accept (someone) as a member of an organization, church, etc.
column11: 接纳（某人）成为某个组织、教会等的成员。
column12: She was received into the church/university.
column13: 她被接纳进入教会/大学。

column10: to suffer (an injury)
column11: 遭受（伤害）
column12: He received [=got] a broken nose when he slipped and fell on the ice.
column13: 他在冰上滑倒时摔断了鼻子。

column10: to be given (a punishment)
column11: 被给予（惩罚）
column12: She received a heavy sentence from the judge.
column13: 她被法官判了重刑。

column10: to experience or take (a medical treatment)
column11: 经历或接受（一种医疗治疗）

column13: 他每周接受一次注射来治疗过敏。

column15: 接受新治疗的患者中，只有一人正在经历严重的副作用。
column16: He received a kidney transplant.
column17: 他接受了肾脏移植。

column10: to get (signals that are sent to a television, radio, etc.)
column11: 接收（发送到电视、收音机等的信号）
column12: We were unable to receive the broadcast.
column13: 我们无法接收到广播。
column14: A satellite receives the signals and then sends them back to earth.
column15: 一颗卫星接收信号，然后将其发送回地球。

column10: to be able to hear (someone who is talking to you on a radio)
column11: 能够听到（通过无线电与你交谈的人）
column12: I'm receiving you loud and clear.
column13: 我收到你的信息，非常清楚。

column10: to be the player or team to which the ball is kicked when play begins
column11: 在比赛开始时成为被踢球的球员或球队

column13: 他们掷硬币获胜并选择接球。
column14: They chose to receive the kickoff.
column15: 他们选择了接球开球。

column10: to buy or take (goods that have been stolen) illegally
column11: 非法购买或收受（被盗的货物）
column12: He was found guilty of receiving stolen goods.
column13: 他被判犯有收受赃物罪。

column10: to tell (someone) that you are grateful for something that he or she has done or given
column11: 告诉（某人）你对他或她所做的事情或所给予的东西表示感激
column12: I thanked her for (giving me) the present.
column13: 我感谢她送给我礼物。

column15: 我要感谢今天所有提供帮助的人。
column16: There's no need to thank me. Anyone would have done the same.
column17: 不必谢我。换作任何人都会这么做的。
